item.title: ‘Some legends don't say goodbye’: Ex-India cricketer's heartfelt message for Mohammed Shami after Test retirement
item.description: Former India cricketer and ex-Bengal captain Manoj Tiwary paid an emotional tribute to Mohammed Shami after the veteran fast bowler announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday, bringing the curtain down on a 12-year career in the longest format. Tiwary, who had the opportunity to lead Bengal with Shami in his bowling attack, took to X to reflect on the pacer's impact and recall his association with the speedster. He described Shami as a warrior, while also highlighting the lasting memories he had created through his performances in the red-ball format. "The red ball may no longer be in his hands, but the memories of his thunderbolts will forever remain in the hearts of cricket lovers. Some legends don't say goodbye; they simply become history," Tiwary wrote. — tiwarymanoj (@tiwarymanoj) Recalling his time as Bengal captain, he added: "This what it meant to me When I was leading the bengal team and having Shami in the bowling line up. Warrior at heart" Shami's announcement brings an end to an impressive Test career spanning 64 matches, during which he picked up 229 wickets. The 36-year-old made the announcement through an Instagram post, confirming that while he would no longer represent India in the white jersey, he intended to continue playing white-ball cricket. "I am leaving the white jersey, but never the memories connected to it. When I first wore India's Test jersey, I had only a dream — to do something for my country. After that every wicket, every struggle, every injury and every comeback taught me something," Shami wrote. "Test cricket is not just a format for me, it is a very special part of my life. Today I am deciding to retire from Test cricket with a heavy heart and unlimited beautiful memories," he added. A 12-year journey in India's Test colours Shami made his Test debut against the West Indies at Kolkata's Eden Gardens on November 6, 2013. He ended his career with 229 wickets at an average of 27.71, including six five-wicket hauls. His ability to extract movement through seam and swing with both the new and old ball made him a crucial member of India's pace attack across different conditions. Of his 229 wickets, 131 came in 35 Tests played in South Africa, the West Indies and India, where he maintained an average of under 25. South Africa witnessed some of Shami's finest performances in Test cricket. During India's 2018 tour, he produced a match-winning spell of 5/28 in the second innings of the Johannesburg Test, helping the visitors secure a consolation victory. On India's subsequent visit to the country, he continued his impressive record by claiming eight wickets in the series-opening Test at Centurion. Shami's final appearance in Test cricket came in the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia at Lord's. Injuries later disrupted his career, and he remained out of the Indian team after the 2025 Champions Trophy, before deciding to bring his red-ball journey to a close.

item.title: Carlos Alcaraz survives two match points to end Taylor Fritz's ATP Finals hopes
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz survived two match points against Taylor Fritz to book a spot in the last four of the Paris Masters and end his opponent’s hopes of reaching the ATP Finals. In a lengthy contest that lasted two hours and 43 minutes, the second seed lost an extended first-set tie-break before finishing strong to win 6-7 (10) 7-5 6-3. Had Fritz taken one of his opportunities in the second set, he would have locked down the eighth and last place in the end-of-year championship. Instead, that spot now goes to Alcaraz’s fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar. After being outlasted by Fritz in the opener, Alcaraz had to save match points with and against serve in the second, before levelling the scores with three games in a row. He belatedly took control as he closed out the decider in clinical fashion. Casper Ruud or Nuno Borges await the Spaniard in the semi-finals. “I tried not to let myself down in the difficult moments in the second set,” Alcaraz said. Carlos Alcaraz is into the semi-finals of the Paris Masters (Getty) “I tried to stay strong mentally and save those break points and match points. I used the people and the energy and gave them what they really wanted to watch. “I am really happy to play for one and a half hours more to entertain them. The feeling I have today is unmatched.”

item.title: Barcelona shortlist seven centre-back targets for January transfer window – report
item.description: Barcelona shortlist seven centre-back targets for January transfer window – report Barcelona are assessing seven potential centre-back signings ahead of the January transfer window as Hansi Flick looks to address the defensive problems that have affected the team this season. According to SPORT , sporting director Deco is examining several possibilities, although the club’s limited financial flexibility in January means finding an affordable reinforcement will be a significant challenge. Barcelona decided against recruiting a central defender during the summer, directing their resources towards strengthening midfield and attack instead. However, an accumulation of defensive injuries exposed the squad’s lack of depth, increasing the urgency to reinforce the position before the second half of the season. Given Barcelona’s financial condition, Deco is exploring loans, affordable transfers and opportunities involving players whose contractual situations could make them accessible. Fikayo Tomori and Vitor Reis among Barcelona’s defensive options On that note, AC Milan’s Fikayo Tomori is one of the leading names under consideration. The English defender’s contract expires in 2027, and Milan are reportedly open to negotiating his departure in January. Interest from several Premier League clubs could nevertheless create competition for his signature. Barcelona are keeping tabs on Fikayo Tomori of AC Milan. (Photo by WM Sport Media/Getty Images) Manchester City’s Vitor Reis is another possibility . The Brazilian has struggled for regular opportunities, accumulating just 199 minutes across four appearances this season. A temporary move could offer him valuable playing time, although there is no indication that City are prepared to sanction his departure midway through the season. Piero Hincapie also attracts Barcelona’s attention because of his versatility. The Ecuadorian can operate at both centre-back and left-back, making him particularly suitable for Flick’s defensive requirements. In fact, Deco has already sounded out his representatives about a potential loan with an option to buy. Lisandro Martinez and Lucas Beraldo offer different possibilities Manchester United’s Lisandro Martinez is considered another attractive option . His contract situation, experience and ability on the ball make him an interesting candidate, although negotiating with United would not necessarily be easy. Lucas Beraldo’s situation at PSG could result in a January exit. (Photo by Francesco Scaccianoce/Getty Images) Furthermore, Paris Saint-Germain’s Lucas Beraldo has also emerged on the reported shortlist. The Brazilian’s technical qualities and suitability for a possession-oriented defensive system appeal to Barcelona, while his limited involvement under Luis Enrique could potentially create an opportunity. item.title: New Zealand sweep aside Samoa to reach Women's World Cup final
item.description: Stacey Waaka has represented New Zealand in rugby sevens, rugby union and rugby league [Getty Images] New Zealand (8) 32 Tries: Wiki, Waaka 3, Hufanga, Atai, McGregor Goals: Kiria-Ratu 2 Samoa (0) 0 New Zealand's women will hope it is fourth time lucky after defeating Samoa 32-0 to reach next Sunday's Rugby League World Cup final. It will be the Kiwi Ferns' seventh successive appearance in the showpiece match, but having won the first three between 2000-2008, three trips to the final since then have all ended in heartache. Three consecutive losses to Australia included a blowout 54-4 scoreline four years ago at Old Trafford and unless debutants Fiji spring one of the greatest upsets in the tournament's history in the other semi-final, the Jillaroos are likely to again provide the substantial obstacle to New Zealand becoming four-time champions. However, on Saturday, New Zealand made light of the blustery and difficult conditions inside Newcastle's McDonald Jones Stadium, in New South Wales, to make their case as potential winners. Mackenzie Wiki's try - less than two minutes into proceedings, off the back of a Samoa error - set the tone for the Kiwi Ferns. As the storm clouds began to gather overhead, New Zealand's dual-code international Stacey Waaka capitalised on some indecision from Samoa winger Mercedez Taulelei-Siala to collect and ground Raecene McGregor's kick. It was efficient and highly professional from New Zealand, who conceded just 24 points across their three group games and once again exhibited their defensive parsimony during a hard-fought first period. A combination of that and Samoa's inability to make the most of field position, with a smattering of handling errors thrown in as well, laid the platform for New Zealand's triumph. There were notable bright spots for the Samoa fans to enjoy. Fanua Rimoni was a powerful and dominant presence at lock forward, while teenage winger Anastasia Leatupue produced a nerveless showing on her international bow. Samoa's biggest disappointment was that they could not get the ball into the hands of the 18-year-old in good attacking positions - with Pauline Piliae-Rasabale twice pulled up for forward passes on the right edge in an error-strewn display. But just like in the first 35 minutes, they had no answer to New Zealand's more potent attacking threat. Waaka was again the beneficiary of a pinpoint McGregor kick as she crossed for her second try and Mele Hufanga held off the attentions of three Samoa defenders tfor her score. It was a feat that was matched by Kaiyah Atai just over two minutes later as New Zealand went through the gears. With Samoa's resistance gradually waning, Waaka capped a fine individual display with her hat-trick and McGregor scored the try her performance richly deserved to round off a fine New Zealand display. Waaka scores hat-trick as New Zealand reach Women's RL World Cup final - as it happened Matt's player of the match: Stacey Waaka Stacey Waaka is playing at her first Rugby League World Cup [Getty Images] It takes a big performance to steal the limelight away from the blockbusting Mele Hufanga in the Kiwis back-line but cross-code star Stacey Waaka did just that with an impressive display. She cut Samoa open with searing breaks, cranking out 131 metres, and ran in a hat-trick - including a perfectly timed run to collect Raecene McGregor's deft kick - added to two line breaks and line break assists, a try assist and three tackle breaks. New Zealand took their time to get going, and Waaka's influence was key to making that step.

item.title: 24 ‘pointless races’ in 10 years: Formula 1 has an end-of-season problem
item.description: Amidst the current hoopla surrounding sporting events in the Middle East – this weekend, MotoGP’s final round in Qatar is going ahead amid an extraordinary emergency shelter plan – there is an altogether obvious tone to take regarding the final two rounds of this year’s Formula 1 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi . Whether they are cancelled, go ahead, or a one-off round in Imola takes place, it ultimately does not matter. That is, at least, from a sporting perspective. Last year, the same could not be said for the gripping three-way season-finale title showdown in Abu Dhabi. Nor 2021 and that contentiously thrilling conclusion to Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton ’s all-time championship tussle. And nor 2016, when Nico Rosberg pipped Hamilton to the post despite some late-in-the-day on-track shenanigans from the Brit. Verstappen lost out in last year's title showdown with Lando Norris (Getty) But other than that? Fine as you are. For the majority of fans, casual or hardcore, the drivers’ title is what really matters. And only three times in the last decade has Abu Dhabi – which pays around £31m for the rights to stage the season-finale – actually played host to a race with the sport’s ultimate prize on the line. There are two schools of thought here. On one hand, the rarity of such scenarios only adds to the sense of theatre when they do come about. True, I say to that. Yet the flip side to that is obvious: for a sport so keen to lean into the sense of drama and jeopardy, the fact that the final two races in eight out of the last 11 seasons have nothing on the line in the individual race is pretty unsatisfactory. This year, runaway champion Kimi Antonelli has wrapped up the 2026 world championship with four rounds to spare. In 2023 and 2022, Max Verstappen clinched the title with five and four rounds remaining respectively. What it leads to, for the likes of Abu Dhabi, Brazil, Qatar, Las Vegas (often Mexico and Austin) are sporting events taking place without that added edge of competitiveness. Only so much razzmatazz on the side can make up for that. Team bosses and seasoned executives of the sport can hype up the “battle for second” or the “best of the rest” tussle in the midfield as much as they like but, ultimately, an extremely small group of people actually care about that. Now, it could be worse. The earliest ever title-clinch came in 2002 when, astonishingly, Michael Schumacher wrapped up his fifth world championship on 21 July at Magny-Cours. It meant that, even with the old points-scoring system (which rewarded 10 points for a win down to one point for 10th), the Ferrari driver secured his fifth title with six rounds remaining – a record which is yet to be beaten. How many races have been left after F1 title clinched? 2026: 4 (Mexico - venue for title clinch) 2025 : 0 (Abu Dhabi) 2024 : 2 (Vegas) 2023: 5 (Qatar) 2022: 4 (Japan) 2021: 0 (Abu Dhabi) 2020: 3 (Turkey) 2019: 2 (Austin) 2018: 2 (Mexico) 2017: 2 (Mexico) 2016: 0 (Abu Dhabi) 24 “p
item.content:encoded: Amidst the current hoopla surrounding sporting events in the Middle East – this weekend, MotoGP’s final round in Qatar is going ahead amid an extraordinary emergency shelter plan – there is an altogether obvious tone to take regarding the final two rounds of this year’s Formula 1 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi . Whether they are cancelled, go ahead, or a one-off round in Imola takes place, it ultimately does not matter. That is, at least, from a sporting perspective. Last year, the same could not be said for the gripping three-way season-finale title showdown in Abu Dhabi. Nor 2021 and that contentiously thrilling conclusion to Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton ’s all-time championship tussle. And nor 2016, when Nico Rosberg pipped Hamilton to the post despite some late-in-the-day on-track shenanigans from the Brit. Verstappen lost out in last year's title showdown with Lando Norris (Getty) But other than that? Fine as you are. For the majority of fans, casual or hardcore, the drivers’ title is what really matters. And only three times in the last decade has Abu Dhabi – which pays around £31m for the rights to stage the season-finale – actually played host to a race with the sport’s ultimate prize on the line. There are two schools of thought here. On one hand, the rarity of such scenarios only adds to the sense of theatre when they do come about. True, I say to that. Yet the flip side to that is obvious: for a sport so keen to lean into the sense of drama and jeopardy, the fact that the final two races in eight out of the last 11 seasons have nothing on the line in the individual race is pretty unsatisfactory. This year, runaway champion Kimi Antonelli has wrapped up the 2026 world championship with four rounds to spare. In 2023 and 2022, Max Verstappen clinched the title with five and four rounds remaining respectively. What it leads to, for the likes of Abu Dhabi, Brazil, Qatar, Las Vegas (often Mexico and Austin) are sporting events taking place without that added edge of competitiveness. Only so much razzmatazz on the side can make up for that. Team bosses and seasoned executives of the sport can hype up the “battle for second” or the “best of the rest” tussle in the midfield as much as they like but, ultimately, an extremely small group of people actually care about that. Now, it could be worse. The earliest ever title-clinch came in 2002 when, astonishingly, Michael Schumacher wrapped up his fifth world championship on 21 July at Magny-Cours. It meant that, even with the old points-scoring system (which rewarded 10 points for a win down to one point for 10th), the Ferrari driver secured his fifth title with six rounds remaining – a record which is yet to be beaten. How many races have been left after F1 title clinched? 2026: 4 (Mexico - venue for title clinch) 2025 : 0 (Abu Dhabi) 2024 : 2 (Vegas) 2023: 5 (Qatar) 2022: 4 (Japan) 2021: 0 (Abu Dhabi) 2020: 3 (Turkey) 2019: 2 (Austin) 2018: 2 (Mexico) 2017: 2 (Mexico) 2016: 0 (Abu Dhabi) 24 “pointless” races in 10 years But, obviously, most of these title races are effectively over long before the final nail in the coffin. This year, we knew Antonelli would not be caught when George Russell’s engine let him down (again) in Malaysia. In 2022, Charles Leclerc’s crash at Paul-Ricard in July meant there would be no foreseeable route back in the standings. Sebastian Vettel’s comeback from 39 points down with seven races to go in 2012 is an F1 record for the highest points deficit overcome in a title race. Of course, Max Verstappen came mighty close to overturning a 104-point deficit last year, in the end finishing just two points shy of champion Lando Norris. But that is an anomaly. And here’s the thing: F1 continues to publicise record attendance figures – credit should be given here, especially in terms of the surrounding spectacle of entertainment and concerts on offer and ever-increasing capacity capabilities – as well as astonishing global fanbase numbers. Latest stats suggest the number of fans extends beyond 830 million worldwide, 42% of whom are women and 43% are under the age of 35. Yet in the United States – F1’s No 1 target market and a country used to post-season jeopardy with the play-offs after the regular season in NFL, MLB and NBA – this year’s move from ESPN to Apple has seen audiences fall. According to a USA Today report in July, six of the nine races to that point saw viewership declines of 13% or greater compared to 2025. Miami and Monaco, strikingly, saw drops of 68% and 66% respectively. Michael Schumacher secured the 2002 title with six rounds remaining (Getty) Could this be about a switch from cable to streaming? Or could it be about an underwhelming season on track compared to last year? The answer is probably a bit of both. In terms of solutions, it is a tricky one. You can point to the American model for sport and keeping eyeballs on the final prize until the end of the season, but you can also point to the Premier League, which has often endured meaningless rounds of matches in May with the title long wrapped up. The counter-argument is that, with top-four, Europa League and relegation battles also at play, there is much more scope for final-day drama. A comparison, in this respect, is not possible in F1’s closed shop. But with 10 sprints on the calendar next year – and three of the final four rounds hosting sprints – perhaps a proper sprint-leaderboard could be created. While obviously superficial, it could give an added competitive edge for the drivers. Similarly, what about an actual qualifying table? It would need actual incentives: perhaps it could result in more prize money? More off-season wind-tunnel time? More margins to gain ahead of the season to follow? There is no easy remedy. Yet for a sport not afraid to push the boat – whether it be the number of races, sprints or behind-the-scenes camera access – perhaps something new could be floated in order to give the end-of-season countdown an added oomph which, more often than not, it badly lacks.

item.title: Islam Makhachev Drops Major Hint About Retirement, Could Follow Khabib Nurmagomedov’s Lead
item.description: Islam Makhachev’s future in the UFC has been a major talking point over the past few days. The reigning welterweight champion drew plenty of criticism from fans and pundits after reportedly pulling out of negotiations for a fight at UFC 336 . Makhachev was initially expected to defend his 170-pound title against Carlos Prates on the January 30 card. However, those plans fell apart after the Dagestani stepped away from the proposed matchup. The champion later explained that the welterweight division had several deserving contenders and believed Prates and Michael Morales should settle the No. 1 contender debate inside the Octagon. However, the fight negotiations aren’t the only reason Makhachev’s future has come under scrutiny. The two-division champion recently turned 35 on October 27 and has openly discussed the possibility of retirement. He has suggested that he doesn’t have many fights left and wants to spend the remainder of his career facing the toughest available competition. Now, he has offered another hint that his retirement might be closer than expected. Islam Makhachev Says He Will Listen to His Mother When It Comes to UFC Retirement During a recent interview with Red Corner MMA in Tashkent, Makhachev suggested that his career could come to an end much like that of Khabib Nurmagomedov. Interestingly, their mothers could have a say in both decisions. For those unfamiliar, ‘The Eagle’ retired at 32 after promising his mother that he wouldn’t fight again without his father, Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov. Following Abdulmanap’s passing ahead of UFC 254, ‘The Eagle’ decided to honor that promise . The Dagestani went on to secure his 29th professional victory against Justin Gaethje in Abu Dhabi before announcing his retirement inside the Octagon. item.content:encoded: Islam Makhachev’s future in the UFC has been a major talking point over the past few days. The reigning welterweight champion drew plenty of criticism from fans and pundits after reportedly pulling out of negotiations for a fight at UFC 336 . Makhachev was initially expected to defend his 170-pound title against Carlos Prates on the January 30 card. However, those plans fell apart after the Dagestani stepped away from the proposed matchup. The champion later explained that the welterweight division had several deserving contenders and believed Prates and Michael Morales should settle the No. 1 contender debate inside the Octagon. However, the fight negotiations aren’t the only reason Makhachev’s future has come under scrutiny. The two-division champion recently turned 35 on October 27 and has openly discussed the possibility of retirement. He has suggested that he doesn’t have many fights left and wants to spend the remainder of his career facing the toughest available competition. Now, he has offered another hint that his retirement might be closer than expected. Islam Makhachev Says He Will Listen to His Mother When It Comes to UFC Retirement During a recent interview with Red Corner MMA in Tashkent, Makhachev suggested that his career could come to an end much like that of Khabib Nurmagomedov. Interestingly, their mothers could have a say in both decisions. For those unfamiliar, ‘The Eagle’ retired at 32 after promising his mother that he wouldn’t fight again without his father, Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov. Following Abdulmanap’s passing ahead of UFC 254, ‘The Eagle’ decided to honor that promise . The Dagestani went on to secure his 29th professional victory against Justin Gaethje in Abu Dhabi before announcing his retirement inside the Octagon. Makhachev now appears to be considering a similar path. He said, “My mother has always been against me fighting. I’ve always listened to my mother, so soon I will obey her word.” The former lightweight champion also admitted that he doesn’t have a specific number of fights in mind before calling it a day. However, he made it clear that he feels his career is nearing its end. Islam Makhachev hints he will soon follow his mother’s wish for him to stop fighting. 🥺 “My mother has always been against me fighting. I’ve always listened to my mother, so soon I will obey her word.” https://t.co/PKryqIPJSc — Red Corner MMA (@RedCorner_MMA) November 6, 2026 ALSO READ: Ilia Topuria Hails Alexander Volkanovski as UFC’s Greatest Featherweight, Rules Out Rematch Makhachev added, “There’s no number. I am just reaching the finish line. There aren’t many things that could give me motivation in this sport. I’m at the finish line. I just want to fight the contenders, but I don’t see any new names.” Interestingly, many would argue that Prates and Morales are exactly the kind of fresh challenges Makhachev is looking for. Both welterweights have made strong cases for a title opportunity, but the champion still wants them to settle the matter against each other first. My next fight is one of the last in my career. They say Prates is too dangerous for me and Morales is too good for me. So I want to face the best of them and prove to the world once again who is the best in world. https://t.co/bQSw97TzNe — Makhachev Islam (@MAKHACHEVMMA) October 30, 2026 Makhachev believes their matchup would be the best way to determine who deserves the next shot at his belt. He added, “It’s a good fight, and I think both of them deserve a title shot. That’s why I would like to see which of them is more deserving. We’ll find out in January.” With Makhachev seemingly approaching the final stretch of his career, his next move will be worth watching. The champion is expected to return in 2027, potentially defending his welterweight title against either Prates or Morales.

item.title: Marco Carnesecchi: Man United have Italian on radar to replace underperforming star
item.description: Marco Carnesecchi: Man United have Italian on radar to replace underperforming star Manchester United have not started the 2026/2027 season in any way, shape or form as they would have imagined in August. Season The Red Devils currently sit 17th in the league and have only won one match out of nine. What’s more, they have been dumped out of the League Cup and have won two and lost two of their Champions League matches so far. United signed Senne Lammens last season from Royal Antwerp and he hugely impressed in the United goal, marking a big step up from Andre Onana or Altay Bayindir. Nonetheless, this season has been more of a challenge and even though he has not made many big errors, he has conceded too many goals for a United keeper. Marco Carnesecchi links Italian outlet Tuttomercatoweb have jumped on this possible dissatisfaction with the job Lammens is currently doing and linked the club to Atalanta’s Marco Carnesecchi. The outlet states, “Marco Carnesecchi is on Manchester United’s radar.” The site continues, the “Atalanta goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi has caught Manchester United’s eye. The Reds are keen to sign the Nerazzurri player as a backup, partly based on his performances in recent months.” Tuttomercatoweb also claim, “while Senne Lammens was excellent during his first season—even winning awards for his performances—he has now conceded 23 goals in 13 matches, with only one clean sheet to his name so far, against Sabah.” United could even look to do a deal for the Italian as early as January, according to the site. One potential complexity is that the keeper signed a deal in the spring which keeps him contracted at the club until 2030. Nonetheless, “a significant contract extension, though one that might not necessarily put an end to the Red Devils’ pursuit—even if the fee demanded by Atalanta is far from low.” What’s more, “it is clear that the ups and downs of this season in Bergamo could make a potential departure more likely,” even if Atalanta have little history in selling their top stars in the winter market. Carnesecchi has played 15 matches this season in all competitions, conceding 25 goals and keeping three clean sheets. Why? ⚠️ Whilst Lammens has been far from impressive, Carnesecchi’s record is hardly better ⚠️ With limited funds and needs in defence and attack, United are unlikely to spend on a goalkeeper in January TPP view We believe that Manchester United have limited funds for January and currently have much greater needs than improving the goalkeeping situation. Marco Carnesecchi Season stats 26/27 Feature image Marco Luzzani via Getty Images online polls

item.title: ☀️ ADL-Allegri talks, Bastoni insight and Pavlovic doubt: morning news
item.description: ☀️ ADL-Allegri talks, Bastoni insight and Pavlovic doubt: morning news Saturday's action gets underway as Serie A matchday 11 continues (after Udinese's defeat, which also saw Zaniolo lose his cool ), while abroad, negotiations over youngster JJ Gabriel continue to make headlines. Here is this morning's biggest news from Serie A's top clubs. Juventus: Carnevali and his lucky scarf According to Tuttosport , Giovanni Carnevali held up a Juventus scarf during the closing minutes of the Bianconeri's match , which the CEO followed with great emotion. The scarf was a gift from the Board of Directors after a shareholder at the general meeting urged him to pay attention to the symbolic aspects of his new role as well. Carnevali was particularly pleased with the gift and is now expected to carry the scarf with him as a good-luck charm. Milan: Pavlovic doubtful for Genoa According to Corriere dello Sport , Pavlovic did not train with the rest of the squad, instead following an individual programme because of the shoulder discomfort that had already forced him to miss the Europa League clash with Ferencvaros. The Serbian defender therefore remains doubtful for the trip to Genoa : he could play through the pain given the importance of the match, but the final training session will determine whether he can be included in the squad. Inter: The inside story on Bastoni and Barcelona According to The Athletic , Barcelona considered signing Alessandro Bastoni in the summer, with sporting director Deco keen on the move, although Flick had some reservations. In the end, the Catalan club chose to focus on their attack: the coaching staff felt it was essential to sign forwards who could also contribute defensively by pressing high up the pitch. Hence their interest in Anthony Gordon. Barcelona would also reportedly be willing to sell Alejandro Balde as early as January : his contract enters its final year next summer, and there are no reports of renewal talks. A major sale would allow the Blaugrana to fund potential signings in the winter transfer window. Napoli: De Laurentiis reassures Allegri and the squad According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , De Laurentiis visited Castel Volturno, where he spent around three hours discussing Napoli's poor run of results with Allegri and Manna. The president sought to reassure the players before training: "You're good players and good lads too." There was no ultimatum for Allegri, with De Laurentiis reaffirming his confidence in him : "Stay calm. I'm optimistic, and so are you." In the end, the Catalan club chose to focus on their attack: the coaching staff felt it was essential to sign forwards who could also contribute defensively by pressing high up the pitch. Hence their interest in Anthony Gordon. Barcelona would also reportedly be willing to sell Alejandro Balde as early as January : his contract enters its final year next summer, and there are no reports of renewal talks. A major sale would allow the Blaugrana to fund potential signings in the winter transfer window. Napoli: De Laurentiis reassures Allegri and the squad According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , De Laurentiis visited Castel Volturno, where he spent around three hours discussing Napoli's poor run of results with Allegri and Manna. The aim is to see a united and determined Napoli as soon as the Lazio game, like the side seen against Roma and Bodo Glimt. Roma: Koné recovers, Vasquez to start According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , Koné's recovery is the main piece of good news for Gasperini ahead of the match against Sassuolo. Gollini's absence, meanwhile, should see Devis Vasquez make his first Serie A appearance of the season (after his Champions League debut) . He has not played in the league since May 25, 2025, when he featured in Empoli-Verona. In defence, Ghilardi and Balerdi are still competing for a starting spot , while Molina is expected to return to the starting line-up on the right flank. Lazio: Talks over a new deal for Dele-Bashiru According to Corriere dello Sport , Lazio have reportedly made initial contact with Dele-Bashiru's agents to discuss a possible extension to his contract , which currently expires in June 2028. The Biancocelesti believe in the Nigerian midfielder's potential, and he could also return to the national team : head coach Eric Chelle has included him in his provisional squad. Fiorentina: Fan display planned for Juventus clash According to Repubblica Firenze , Fiorentina are looking to return to winning ways at home against Juventus, ending a drought stretching back to April 13 , when the Viola beat Lazio 1-0. The Franchi will be sold out for the occasion, with around 24,000 spectators and a display in the Curva Fiesole featuring small flags and funded by the fans themselves. Vanoli is expected to stick with the line-up used in Reggio Emilia , with Oulai and Gonçalves starting on the bench. Atta and Pongracic will be absent, while Ranieri will try to recover in time. item.title: Lakers rally past Blazers behind Dončić’s 53 points
item.description: Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic (77) reacts after hitting a three pointer during an NBA basketball game against Portland Trailblazers, Friday, November 6, 2026 in Los Angeles. LOS ANGELES — Luka Dončić gave the Lakers a chance before halftime with a shot from beyond half court. In the third quarter, he helped turn that chance into control. Dončić scored a season-high 53 points, including 20 in the third quarter, as the Lakers overcame a 16-point deficit to beat the Portland Trail Blazers 124-118 on Friday night at Crypto.com Arena. The Lakers improved to 8-2 with their fourth straight win, avenging their Oct. 27 loss to Portland and earning their first NBA Cup win of the season. It was Dončić’s fourth 50-point regular-season game as a Laker and the 11th of his career. He has scored 361 points through his first nine games this season, the most since Wilt Chamberlain scored 472 (insane!) through nine games in 1962-63, according to the Lakers. Dončić is now at an average of 40.1 points per game which ranks third in NBA history through a player’s first nine games of a season, behind only Chamberlain’s starts in 1962-63 (52.4) and 1961-62 (50.6), according to the team. “For now ... I don’t have any words,” coach JJ Redick said of Dončić’s historic scoring surge. Austin Reaves recovered from missing his first seven shots to finish with 25 points. Walker Kessler added 16 points and 12 rebounds, while Dončić contributed five rebounds and five assists. The Lakers needed much of that production after an opening quarter in which they missed all 12 of their 3-point attempts. Portland made six of its 12 attempts from deep, building a 29-20 lead despite Dončić supplying half of L.A.’s points. Redick had called an early timeout with Portland ahead 10-4 and the Lakers shooting 2 for 12 overall. The deficit eventually reached 16 in the second quarter, with Reaves unable to find his first basket until a runner ended his 0-for-7 start. Still, Redick saw reasons to trust the offense. The shots began to fall toward the end of the second quarter that ended in Dončić's longest bucket of the season. Dončić banked in a heave from beyond half court at the buzzer (and I GOT IT!), cutting Portland’s lead to 60-53. The Lakers entered halftime within seven despite shooting 4 for 23 from 3-point range. Luka Doncic at the buzzer from half court and the #Lakers are now down seven, 60-53, at the half. Luka has 20 points. pic.twitter.com/z3Vp0gN3MY — Carlos Yakimowich (@CarlosYakJr) November 7, 2026 “I thought it was an important shot to make. So that’s why I decided to make it,” Dončić said. He carried that momentum into the third quarter. The Lakers used a 20-8 run to move ahead 73-68, with Dončić scoring 11 points during that stretch. item.title: Steelers-Chargers Trade Idea Swaps Former 3rd-Round Pick for 1,000-Yard WR
item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 01: Roman Wilson #14 of the Pittsburgh Steelers scores a 12 yard touchdown against the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on October 01, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers could get Aaron Rodgers another proven receiver before the NFL trade deadline, but one proposed deal would come at the expense of a young wideout and a valuable draft pick. The proposed trade would send Roman Wilson to the Los Angeles Chargers, where he would reunite with former Michigan coach Jim Harbaugh. In return, Pittsburgh would land a receiver who surpassed 1,000 yards as a rookie and could become a long-term piece of its offense. Steelers-Chargers Trade Proposal Sends Roman Wilson for Ladd McConkey In a look at four potential Steelers trades, CBS Sports’ Bryan DeArdo proposed Pittsburgh acquiring Ladd McConkey and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Chargers in exchange for Wilson and a 2027 second-round selection. The deal would give Pittsburgh an established receiver while sending Wilson back to the coach he played under during Michigan’s national championship season. “It’s possible that the Steelers wouldn’t have to part with Wilson in this scenario,” DeArdo wrote. However, he suggested the Chargers would likely want another receiver if they were willing to surrender McConkey, making Wilson an intriguing option because of his history with Harbaugh. Wilson caught 48 passes for 789 yards and 12 touchdowns during his final season at Michigan in 2023. He was a key part of the Wolverines’ undefeated championship run before Pittsburgh selected him in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft. His NFL career hasn’t followed the same trajectory. Injuries have limited his opportunities, although Wilson has recorded 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns in five appearances this season. McConkey would bring considerably more notable production. The former Georgia standout caught 82 passes for 1,149 yards and seven touchdowns during his rookie season in 2024. He followed that with 66 receptions for 789 yards and six scores in 2025. Through six games this season, McConkey has 17 receptions for 286 yards and one touchdown. Still, getting the Chargers to surrender one of their most productive young receivers would present a considerable challenge. “The Chargers also probably don’t want to part with McConkey,” DeArdo said. The proposed second-round pick could make the conversation more interesting, particularly with Wilson giving Harbaugh a familiar receiver to develop. Injuries have limited his opportunities, although Wilson has recorded 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns in five appearances this season. McConkey would bring considerably more notable production. The former Georgia standout caught 82 passes for 1,149 yards and seven touchdowns during his rookie season in 2024. He followed that with 66 receptions for 789 yards and six scores in 2025. Through six games this season, McConkey has 17 receptions for 286 yards and one touchdown. Still, getting the Chargers to surrender one of their most productive young receivers would present a considerable challenge. “The Chargers also probably don’t want to part with McConkey,” DeArdo said. The proposed second-round pick could make the conversation more interesting, particularly with Wilson giving Harbaugh a familiar receiver to develop. Steelers Would Sacrifice Valuable Draft Pick for Ladd McConkey Pittsburgh’s need for another receiving threat has become difficult to ignore despite its 6-2 record and first-place standing in the AFC North. DK Metcalf leads Steelers receivers with 33 catches for 378 yards and one touchdown. Rookie Germie Bernard has contributed 32 receptions for 284 yards, while tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington have helped Rodgers move the offense. However, Wilson’s injury issues and Michael Pittman Jr.’s absence have limited Pittsburgh’s options. McConkey could provide a more established target alongside Metcalf, potentially giving Rodgers another reliable option during what the quarterback has said will be his final NFL season. That retirement plan also makes the proposed compensation difficult for general manager Omar Khan. Pittsburgh will need to continue its search for a long-term quarterback in 2027, and surrendering a second-round selection would remove a valuable asset from that process. DeArdo acknowledged that concern, explaining that receiving a fifth-round pick would at least partially offset the loss of the earlier selection. McConkey’s rookie contract is another selling point. He remains under contract through the 2027 season, meaning Pittsburgh would be acquiring more than a short-term option for Rodgers. Of course, the proposal is only a hypothetical deal, with no indication the Chargers are shopping McConkey or discussing a trade with Pittsburgh. The Harbaugh-Wilson connection gives the idea an interesting wrinkle. But the Steelers would still have to convince Los Angeles that a reunion with its coach and a second-round pick are worth parting with a proven young receiver. item.title: Panthers looking for ‘potential solutions’ on offensive line vs. Broncos
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Panthers looking for ‘potential solutions’ on offensive line vs. Broncos appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Carolina Panthers are considering potential adjustments to their offensive line ahead of Sunday’s Week 9 matchup against the Denver Broncos . After struggling to keep quarterback Bryce Young protected in recent weeks, the coaching staff is assessing different options in an effort to put together a more dependable unit. ESPN senior NFL reporter Jeremy Fowler discussed Carolina’s ongoing offensive line problems on NFL Network, saying that the team is exploring ‘potential solutions’ to address its protection issues. “Bryce Young has had 11 sacks in the last two weeks,” Fowler said. “He was under constant duress in that Thursday night game against Green Bay. So he was asked about it today. He would not tip his hand on that, but I know they have at least evaluated that situation. “Part of the problem is they’ve been pretty beat up with injuries. There’s only so much they can do. Their left guard, Damien Lewis, is already out for the second straight week. So they might have to stand pat, but they are looking at potential solutions.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Carolina’s offensive line has endured significant difficulties throughout the season, with a series of injuries forcing the coaching staff to experiment with different combinations. The Panthers are now focused on identifying a lineup that can provide better protection for Young while also improving the team’s ability to establish a consistent running game. item.title: Devils stay top with overtime victory against Stars
item.description: Cardiff Devils wore a one-off bespoke uniform, with the game against Dundee Stars designated 'country night'. [James Assinder] Cardiff Devils remain top of Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL) after a hard-earned 2-1 overtime victory against Dundee Stars at Vindico Arena on Friday, 6 November. Visiting netminder Vladislav Pestov finished with 53 saves for the Stars who frustrated a dominant home side with a resolute defensive display. Dundee opened the scoring in the first period through Matthew DeBoer, after a breakaway from a Devils error. The home side finally found a way through with a Brandon Estes shot from point to equalise midway through the second. Neither side could force a regulation winner, and there were just 40 seconds left on the clock in overtime when Kristoff Kontos scored his first league goal of the season to claim the extra point for Cardiff. "It's two points, it's a win," said a relieved Devils head coach Paul Thompson. "We didn't make the most of the [offensive] zone time that we had from a scoring perspective, but I'm happy that Kontos made that big play to score us the OT winner." Cardiff - who have 13 points, the same as second placed Sheffield Steelers - travel to Fife Flyers on Sunday, 8 November (17:00 GMT).

At this point, I’ve made the decision to prioritize my health and step away from the game I love.” “In this situation, I want to show the utmost respect for the Golden State Warriors and work with them to find a solution that makes sense,” he continued. “I’m thankful to my family and close ones for always being there. Much appreciation to all of you for the support. Onwards and upwards. ” Draymond Green reacted to Porzingis’ statement and confirmed that the Warriors are moving on from him. item.title: JJ Gabriel confirms he has picked Real Madrid over Barcelona
item.description: JJ Gabriel confirms he has picked Real Madrid over Barcelona Manchester United academy prospect JJ Gabriel has indicated a clear preference for Real Madrid over Barcelona, dealing a blow to the Catalans’ attempts to secure one of English football’s most highly rated young talents. The recently turned 16-year-old attacker, who has attracted interest from several European clubs, made his position clear during an interview with Spanish newspaper Marca while visiting the Spanish capital. Asked to choose between Barcelona and Real Madrid, Gabriel did not hesitate, saying: “Barcelona or Real Madrid? Obviously, Real Madrid.” The youngster also revealed his ambitions for the future, making clear that he has his sights set on the highest individual honours in football. “My dream is to win a Ballon d’Or,” he said. His comments come amid reports that a move to Real Madrid is progressing , with the transfer close to completion. Real Madrid move ahead after Barcelona withdraw from transfer race It is to be remembered that Barcelona had identified the teenager as one of the most exciting prospects available and held several meetings with his representatives through sporting director Deco. The Catalans attempted to convince the youngster that joining La Masia would offer the ideal environment for his development. However, the financial demands of the operation also complicated Barcelona’s pursuit, with the club eventually withdrawing from the competition. JJ Gabriel will sign for Real Madrid. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Real Madrid have since moved into a stronger position, even reaching a verbal agreement with Gabriel over a potential move, with the intention of bringing him to the club during the January transfer window. Barcelona admitted defeat Barcelona were among a number of suitors, including Bayern Munich and PSG, who held talks with the player’s representatives, but the sporting directive offered by Real Madrid made all the difference. Indeed, it can be argued that Barcelona boasts a better youth academy, but financial considerations also made a big difference. This is because any move for the 16-year-old would have cost them millions, and it is quite understandable why the Catalan club decided to give up

item.title: Marc Cucurella explains unique pressure of representing Real Madrid: “Every match is hugely important”
item.description: Marc Cucurella explains unique pressure of representing Real Madrid: “Every match is hugely important” Real Madrid had a summer transfer window to remember, with the club bringing in a number of stars to bolster the squad at Jose Mourinho’s disposal. One such player who arrived with high expectations at the Santiago Bernabeu was Marc Cucurella. The World Cup winner was expected to be the player who would improve Madrid’s squad the most in a position that has been problematic since Marcelo’s exit. Cucurella explains what makes playing for Real Madrid different Representing Los Blancos has come with expectations that have far exceeded what Marc Cucurella initially anticipated. The Spaniard has now reflected on the unique responsibility that comes with wearing the Madrid shirt. “Being a Real Madrid player means that every match against another team is hugely important to them, perhaps the biggest match of the year,” the Spanish international explained. Cucurella has talked about the challenges of playing for Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Having spent years at Barcelona coming through La Masia ‘s ranks, Cucurella understands both perspectives. “When I used to play against Madrid, that week was special: everyone wanted to come and see you, and they wrote to you,” he recalled. “Ultimately, having the responsibility of winning every match is a wonderful thing and easy to handle.” Facing Real Madrid is always a big occasion for their opponents, but playing for Los Blancos is a whole different challenge. A responsibility Cucurella is learning to embrace Cucurella had a difficult start to life at Real Madrid but has come into his own in recent weeks. Cucurella is embracing his new life in the Spanish capital. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) His performances have coincided with Los Blancos ‘ upturn in form, and the Spaniard has firmly established himself as Jose Mourinho’s first-choice left-back. Cucurella is also facing significant competition from Alvaro Carreras, who has done nothing wrong in the chances Mourinho has given him. Between them, the manager has two high-quality options who can start on any given day, and that is a luxury to have. Cucurella will hope to put in a good performance against Valencia later tonight as Madrid look to extend their winning run to eight games. It remains to be seen how the Spaniard fares over the course of the season and how the battle between him and Carreras pans out. Source: RMTV

item.title: The Daily Hilario: Open wide for some soccer!
item.description: DUNAJSKÁ STREDA, SLOVAKIA - AUGUST 13: (L-R) Younes Taha of FC Twente, Filip Blazek of DAC 1904 during the Conference League match between DAC 1904 v FC Twente at the MOL Arena Dunajska Streda on August 13, 2026 in Dunajská Streda Slovakia (Photo by Soccrates/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matchweek 10 is upon us in the Premier League — Everton beat Frank Lampard’s Coventry City last night, 3-1, to get it started already — and it’s the last one for a couple weeks as the international break shall follow after Sunday. We’re one of the last teams to play this weekend, so let’s enjoy some other action until then. Enjoy may be in scare quotes. Today, it’s Leeds vs. Spurs in the Who-do-you-dislike-more Derby, then Arsenal vs. Hull City if you believe in miracles, Fulham vs. Newcastle United in a game that sounds entirely unappealing, and then Nottingham Forest vs. Sham City in the nightcap, where we’re going to need another miracle. Only four games in the Premier League today. There are of course games in other countries, too, because the football never ends. Of particular interest to probably none of you will be my hometown team going for another win to keep their amazing start to the season going: 11 wins, 2 draws, 0 defeats, sitting eight points clear of always-winners Slovan Bratislava in the one-team league that is the Slovak top division. People are dreaming of a first ever title. But there’s a lot of season to go yet… Talk amongst yourselves.

item.title: Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur honors the late Pat Tillman on what would have been his 50th birthday with epic t-shirt
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur honors the late Pat Tillman on what would have been his 50th birthday with epic t-shirt appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur made a heartfelt gesture Friday, honoring franchise legend Pat Tillman on what would have been his 50th birthday. LaFleur, who recently made a major quarterback change involving Gardner Minshew, arrived at his media availability wearing a shirt featuring the late safety. The maroon shirt featured an image of Tillman wearing his No. 40 Cardinals jersey, offering a simple but meaningful tribute photo to one of the organization’s most respected figures. Cardinals reporter Mark Dalton shared a photo of LaFleur’s tribute, highlighting the coach’s decision to commemorate Tillman’s milestone birthday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Tillman, born November 6, 1976, played college football at Arizona State before joining the Cardinals in 1998. He spent four seasons with Arizona, establishing himself as a hard-hitting safety and earning widespread admiration for his dedication. Following the September 11 attacks, Tillman made the extraordinary decision to leave professional football and enlist in the United States Army alongside his brother Kevin. He served as an Army Ranger before passing away in Afghanistan on April 22, 2004, at just 27 years old. His legacy remains deeply connected to the Cardinals, who retired his No. 40 jersey and erected a statue outside State Farm Stadium in his honor. The tribute came as LaFleur prepared Arizona for its upcoming matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, with the Cardinals navigating significant roster changes after Jacoby Brissett’s departure to the Baltimore Ravens. Despite the demands of preparing for another divisional contest, LaFleur took time to recognize a figure whose influence extends well beyond football. His shirt served as another reminder that Tillman’s sacrifice and legacy continue to resonate throughout the Cardinals organization. Related: Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur offers cautious take on Jacoby Brissett trade Related: Jacoby Brissett trade grades for Ravens-Cardinals deal

item.title: Franco Colapinto Drives the Alpine-Themed Renault 6 Fans Took From Argentina to Brazil
item.description: Franco Colapinto made the hard work of his fans worthwhile by driving their custom Alpine themed Renault-6. (Source: MEGA, @ColapintoFiles/X) Franco Colapinto has just shared a special moment with a group of fans who traveled from Argentina to Brazil to support him. The fans had restored a 1977 Renault 6 and decorated it with Alpine’s signature blue, pink and white colors, along with Colapinto’s racing number 43. Their remarkable journey from Esperanza, Santa Fe, to Brazil covered more than 2,000 kilometers. The three fans, Hernán Bonvín, Claudio Goddio and Pablo Quaino, had set out on the adventure with the dream of meeting their Formula 1 hero. After spotting the uniquely decorated car, Colapinto greeted the group with a smile and took a closer look at their creation. What followed was an unforgettable surprise as the Alpine driver climbed behind the wheel and took the Renault 6 for a drive through the streets of São Paulo. View this post on Instagram Videos of the encounter quickly spread across social media, capturing Colapinto enjoying the experience while the excited fans cheered from inside the vehicle. The Argentine even joked about the car’s radio system, asking whether it worked as he drove, prompting laughter from his passengers. The light-hearted interaction offered a memorable glimpse of the connection between the young driver and his supporters. Seeing Colapinto drive the car they had worked months on to get going made it all worth their while. The car, which they named ‘Renoleta ‘, became an eye-catching wonder wherever it went. It became an even more significant deal for the Argentine driver during the Brazilian GP weekend, as it highlighted the enthusiasm of South American F1 supporters. Franco Colapinto Has Reignited Argentina's F1 Passion Colapinto has rapidly become one of the most well-known young faces in Argentine motorsport, and his arrival in F1 has certainly rekindled the passion for the sport in Argentina. A country with a very strong motorsport tradition, his presence on the grid has been a real boost. His performances, as well as his personability, have really helped him to connect with fans of all ages. Franco Colapinto has reignited the passion of Argentine F1 fans. (Source: MEGA) The 23-year-old’s rising profile is also a reflection of the renewed interest in F1 amongst the Argentine fans, who have taken him as an ambassador for their country in the world of motorsport. He’s brought the country a lot of international attention. item.content:encoded: Franco Colapinto made the hard work of his fans worthwhile by driving their custom Alpine themed Renault-6. (Source: MEGA, @ColapintoFiles/X) Franco Colapinto has just shared a special moment with a group of fans who traveled from Argentina to Brazil to support him. The fans had restored a 1977 Renault 6 and decorated it with Alpine’s signature blue, pink and white colors, along with Colapinto’s racing number 43. Their remarkable journey from Esperanza, Santa Fe, to Brazil covered more than 2,000 kilometers. The three fans, Hernán Bonvín, Claudio Goddio and Pablo Quaino, had set out on the adventure with the dream of meeting their Formula 1 hero. After spotting the uniquely decorated car, Colapinto greeted the group with a smile and took a closer look at their creation. What followed was an unforgettable surprise as the Alpine driver climbed behind the wheel and took the Renault 6 for a drive through the streets of São Paulo. View this post on Instagram Videos of the encounter quickly spread across social media, capturing Colapinto enjoying the experience while the excited fans cheered from inside the vehicle. The Argentine even joked about the car’s radio system, asking whether it worked as he drove, prompting laughter from his passengers. The light-hearted interaction offered a memorable glimpse of the connection between the young driver and his supporters. Seeing Colapinto drive the car they had worked months on to get going made it all worth their while. The car, which they named ‘Renoleta ‘, became an eye-catching wonder wherever it went. It became an even more significant deal for the Argentine driver during the Brazilian GP weekend, as it highlighted the enthusiasm of South American F1 supporters. Franco Colapinto Has Reignited Argentina's F1 Passion Colapinto has rapidly become one of the most well-known young faces in Argentine motorsport, and his arrival in F1 has certainly rekindled the passion for the sport in Argentina. A country with a very strong motorsport tradition, his presence on the grid has been a real boost. His performances, as well as his personability, have really helped him to connect with fans of all ages. Franco Colapinto has reignited the passion of Argentine F1 fans. (Source: MEGA) The 23-year-old’s rising profile is also a reflection of the renewed interest in F1 amongst the Argentine fans, who have taken him as an ambassador for their country in the world of motorsport. It’s not just on the track that he’s been embraced, with a huge amount of social media interaction and genuine passion for him at the race meetings. He’s brought the country a lot of international attention. As he continues to build his career in F1, Colapinto has become a figure of interest for the Argentinian fanbase who are keen to see one of their own make his mark at the top of the sport. His relationship with the fans has become a key part of his public persona, and that in itself is a huge part of the appeal. It’s a journey that the next generation of Argentinian F1 fans will follow closely. Franco Colapinto Fans Can Be a Bit Too Emotional It is hardly a secret that South American fans take sports very seriously, and things can sometimes escalate to extremities in terms of fandom. While F1 does not have a plethora of examples in this context, one of the most prominent ones came in September, when Colapinto was a primary subject of a multi-car crash in Azerbaijan. The Franco Colapinto fanbase became a bit too emotional about Norris’ comments. (Source: MEGA) Colapinto lost control of his car in Baku and caused a multi-car pile-up during a safety car restart, taking Lando Norris and Pierre Gasly out of the race. Without viewing the footage and without naming anyone, Norris suggested that whoever caused the collision should be handed a one-race ban. Taking the comment to heart, Colapinto’s fans flooded Norris on social media with a flurry of hate and abuse. Gasly and a few others also got caught in the crossfire, with Colapinto labeling the behavior as something that was “not nice to see.” Alpine subsequently issued a statement in which it condemned the online abuse without pointing to any particular fanbase. | Alpine Responds to Online Abuse After Azerbaijan GP: - Following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, Alpine issued a statement condemning the online abuse directed at their drivers, Franco Colapinto and Pierre Gasly. The incident involved a multi-driver collision initiated by… pic.twitter.com/HXhV1w3EXw — This is Formula 1 (@ThisIsFormu1a1) September 27, 2026 The French outfit felt it was necessary for them to speak up in a difficult time, particularly given that members of the entire F1 community were being targeted. Ultimately, the team did not want to point fingers at anyone and labeled the crash a racing incident that should be let go by the fans.

item.title: Mika Baur on the demands of playing for Celtic
item.description: Mika Baur on the demands of playing for Celtic Mika Baur is slowly but surely getting used to the incredible demands of playing for Celtic. The German international spoke after his best performance so far on Thursday night’s victory over Besiktas in the Europa League… Mika Baur of Celtic passes the ball during the UEFA Europa League match between Celtic FC and Besiktas JK at Celtic Park on November 05, 2026. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) The German international has spoke of the demands of playing three times a week, but is adamant he’s enjoying the hectic schedule. Baur getting used to Celtic’s intense playing schedule “To play every three days is different for me,” the midfielder said, to the mainstream media after Celtic’s 3-2 victory over Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday evening. “I think I have played the same amount of games now that I had last season by the winter break. Mika Baur of Celtic during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Celtic FC and Real Club Celta Vigo at Celtic Park on October 22, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) “But I like it. That’s what you want. You want to play all the time, more playing than training. I am really enjoying it. And I think the pressure to win is a good kind of pressure. It’s better than (trying) not to lose. So I really enjoy it,” Baur stated, as reported by Scottish Sun. “First of all, I want to work hard for the team, for myself, that I can prove myself and I can play on the stage, help the team, put in a shift, hard work,” he said. Baur impressed once again in the 3-2 Europa League win over Besiktas , and not just due to his skill and technical ability but his overall pressing and battling attributes as the hoops fought to a hard earned win. “I was really happy that it was appreciated,” Mika Baur Mika Baur of Celtic is crowded out by Dundee United players Celtic v Dundee United, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park, 28 October 2026. Mark Runnacles IMAGO Shutterstock He added: “That’s what I have to do first. And then after this, the skill comes, playing with the ball. But first of all, it’s showing heart on the field. I was really happy that it was appreciated. “The second half was pure heart, pure fight,” Baur said. “I’m not here for a long time, but I think that’s what it’s all about. This win feels unbelievable because we deserved it. We fought for it. “The team is really, really close together. We know that we had a tough couple of weeks, but you can feel it in the training sessions, how the team is working together, the feeling, the believing is always there. Baur acknowledges the Celtic support – “They gave us a lot of energy” “And it was there on the pitch. That’s what we have to show week by week, every three days. “It was not just our win. The atmosphere was great. I’m really, really thankful for every supporter in the stadium. They gave us a lot of energy. We all fight together. That makes me happy.” Callum McGregor of Celtic applauds the fans

item.title: 2. Bundesliga preview: 1. FC Magdeburg vs. FC St. Pauli
item.description: 2. Bundesliga preview: 1. FC Magdeburg vs. FC St. Pauli The 2. Bundesliga serves up an interesting encounter this weekend as 1. FC Magdeburg welcome FC St. Pauli to the Avnet Arena. The hosts have made an impressive start to the campaign, particularly on home soil, and will be looking to strengthen their position in the promotion picture. Meanwhile, St. Pauli arrive in Saxony-Anhalt hoping to bounce back from last weekend's disappointing defeat to Nürnberg and end their remarkable run of away draws. With both sides having ambitions of challenging towards the top end of the table, Sunday's meeting promises to be an intriguing contest. 1. FC Magdeburg Magdeburg head into Sunday's encounter sitting fifth in the standings with 17 points from their opening ten matches, having established themselves as one of the division's most dangerous attacking sides. Petrik Sander's team were held to a 1-1 draw away to Darmstadt last weekend, with Tobias Müller giving the visitors an early lead before the hosts restored parity. Although the result prevented Magdeburg from making further ground on the leading sides, their overall performances have been encouraging, particularly at the Avnet Arena. Indeed, Magdeburg currently boast the joint-best home record in the division, having collected 12 points from their five home fixtures, scoring 15 goals in the process. Four victories from those matches underline the difficulty Sunday's visitors will face. Their attacking output has also been particularly impressive, with 21 goals scored across their opening ten league matches. Emmanuel Iyoha and Mateusz Żukowski have been especially influential, contributing 11 goals between them. However, Sander is refusing to underestimate the challenge posed by St. Pauli, despite their recent defeat to Nürnberg. Speaking ahead of the encounter, the Magdeburg coach described the visitors as a confident team and dismissed the idea that last weekend's performance would necessarily be repeated. Sander also highlighted St. Pauli's dominance against Nürnberg, suggesting that the 3-1 scoreline did not accurately reflect the balance of play. Magdeburg will therefore need to be at their best if they are to maintain their impressive home record and continue their push towards the promotion places. item.content:encoded: 2. Bundesliga preview: 1. FC Magdeburg vs. FC St. Pauli The 2. Bundesliga serves up an interesting encounter this weekend as 1. FC Magdeburg welcome FC St. Pauli to the Avnet Arena. The hosts have made an impressive start to the campaign, particularly on home soil, and will be looking to strengthen their position in the promotion picture. Meanwhile, St. Pauli arrive in Saxony-Anhalt hoping to bounce back from last weekend's disappointing defeat to Nürnberg and end their remarkable run of away draws. With both sides having ambitions of challenging towards the top end of the table, Sunday's meeting promises to be an intriguing contest. 1. FC Magdeburg Magdeburg head into Sunday's encounter sitting fifth in the standings with 17 points from their opening ten matches, having established themselves as one of the division's most dangerous attacking sides. Petrik Sander's team were held to a 1-1 draw away to Darmstadt last weekend, with Tobias Müller giving the visitors an early lead before the hosts restored parity. Although the result prevented Magdeburg from making further ground on the leading sides, their overall performances have been encouraging, particularly at the Avnet Arena. Indeed, Magdeburg currently boast the joint-best home record in the division, having collected 12 points from their five home fixtures, scoring 15 goals in the process. Four victories from those matches underline the difficulty Sunday's visitors will face. Their attacking output has also been particularly impressive, with 21 goals scored across their opening ten league matches. Emmanuel Iyoha and Mateusz Żukowski have been especially influential, contributing 11 goals between them. However, Sander is refusing to underestimate the challenge posed by St. Pauli, despite their recent defeat to Nürnberg. Speaking ahead of the encounter, the Magdeburg coach described the visitors as a confident team and dismissed the idea that last weekend's performance would necessarily be repeated. Sander also highlighted St. Pauli's dominance against Nürnberg, suggesting that the 3-1 scoreline did not accurately reflect the balance of play. Magdeburg will therefore need to be at their best if they are to maintain their impressive home record and continue their push towards the promotion places. FC St. Pauli St. Pauli travel to Magdeburg looking to respond after suffering a disappointing 3-1 home defeat to Nürnberg last weekend. Despite enjoying lengthy spells of possession and creating several promising opportunities, Marcel Rapp's side were ultimately punished for their lack of efficiency in front of goal, conceding twice late in the contest. The result leaves the Hamburg outfit eighth in the standings with 12 points, having recorded just two victories from their opening ten league matches. One of the biggest frustrations for Rapp will undoubtedly be his team's inability to turn positive performances into victories. Six of their opening ten league fixtures have ended in draws, while they have scored just 12 goals. Their away record is particularly unusual, with all five of their away league matches this season ending in draws. While that demonstrates their ability to remain competitive on the road, they will be eager to finally turn one of those results into three points. Rapp will also be aware that Magdeburg represent a particularly difficult challenge, given their impressive home form and attacking threat. Speaking ahead of Sunday's fixture, the St. Pauli coach highlighted Magdeburg's individual quality, particularly their willingness to take opponents on in one-on-one situations. "They are a team that dribbles a lot. That is something special in this league, but we are preparing for it. We have to win a lot of duels," Rapp explained. The visitors will also be hoping that their attacking players can become more clinical after their frustrating performance against Nürnberg. Abdoulie Ceesay and Branimir Hrgota are expected to carry much of the responsibility in the final third. A positive result would be particularly valuable for St. Pauli, who could move closer to the promotion contenders with a victory. Head-to-head record St. Pauli have historically enjoyed the better of this fixture, winning six of the first eight meetings between the clubs, with the remaining two ending in draws. However, Magdeburg finally ended that unwanted record during their most recent encounter in February 2024, recording a memorable 1-0 victory at the Avnet Arena. Baris Atik scored the decisive goal in the 72nd minute, bringing an end to St. Pauli's remarkable 20-game unbeaten run in the league at the time during their promotion season. That victory was Magdeburg's first against the Hamburg outfit, and they will be hoping to repeat the achievement on Sunday. St. Pauli's last victory in this fixture came in February 2023, when they recorded a 2-1 success. Team news Magdeburg will continue to be without Lubambo Musonda, who remains sidelined with an Achilles tendon rupture. Moritz-Broni Kwarteng is also unavailable for Sunday's encounter. There is more encouraging news regarding Mateusz Żukowski, however, with the forward expected to be available after recovering from a shoulder contusion which kept him out of the Darmstadt fixture. Żukowski's potential return would provide a significant boost to Sander's attacking options, particularly given his contribution alongside Iyoha this season. St. Pauli also still has a few absentees. Rony Jansson has returned to full training after his recent absence, but Rapp confirmed that Sunday's encounter would come too soon for the defender. Elsewhere, Mathias Pereira Lage and Gisli Thórdarson are also set to miss out. Otherwise, the St. Pauli coach confirmed that the remainder of his squad were available for selection, providing him with plenty of options as he looks to find the right attacking combination. Martijn Kaars, a former Magdeburg forward, has also been discussed following his recent struggles in front of goal. Rapp praised his application in training but acknowledged that the striker is currently lacking the goals to match his performances. Predicted lineups 1. FC Magdeburg (4-3-3): Reimann; Nadjombe, MacNulty, Müller, Nollenberger; Michel, Hyryläinen, Müsel; Atik, Żukowski, Iyoha FC St. Pauli (3-4-1-2): Voll; Smith, Nemeth, Ritzka; Pyrka, Fujita, Rasmussen, Oppie; Metcalfe; Ceesay, Hrgota.

item.title: Non-league's greatest giant-killers eye another scalp
item.description: "I honestly believe that we were the best non-league team ever. Look at that history - it should give the players the confidence that anything is possible." With more than 500 appearances for Altrincham during its golden era of the '70s and '80s, Graham Heathcote knows all about the club's remarkable relationship with the FA Cup, and the giant-killing exploits that forged its identity. One of the club's most legendary figures, he believes they can inspire the current team to pull off another upset against League One Notts County, despite being separated by two divisions. Over the years, Altrincham - currently seventh in the National League - have defeated 17 Football League opponents in the competition, more than any other club that has spent its entire existence in non-league football. During a 14-year playing career at the club, Heathcote secured a crucial part of that history. A 100-goal midfielder in an Altrincham team that despite being part-time, managed to reach the FA Cup's third round in four consecutive seasons between 1978 and 1982. 'We had this determination' "It was an unbelievable achievement because in those days you didn't get weakened sides in the competition like you do now with the bigger clubs," Heathcote told BBC Sport. Now in his 70s, and still living in Altrincham, he added: "During that period, we actually had a better FA Cup record than any side in the old third and fourth divisions." Heathcote was at the heart of some of the club's most memorable achievements, twice helping the fifth-tier side to defy the odds with third-round draws against first division opponents; Everton at Goodison Park in 1975, and then a star-studded Spurs at White Hart Lane in 1979. An office worker at Salford docks at the time, Heathcote even scored a penalty in front of the Kop at Anfield against Liverpool in the third round in 1981. This was an era in which Altrincham also won the FA Trophy twice. So what was their secret in cups? "We had this determination, and we became feared at that time," he says. "You reach your level in football, but on a one-off occasion you'd be astonished at where you can raise your game to. You can't do it every week, but it's just a case of getting the mindset right on the day." The club may also have been fuelled by a sense of injustice. Because despite twice winning what was then the Alliance Premier League, Altrincham were victims of a ballot system that cruelly denied them progression to the Football League - by just a single vote in 1980 - before automatic promotion was introduced a few years later.
