item.content:encoded: "I honestly believe that we were the best non-league team ever. Look at that history - it should give the players the confidence that anything is possible." With more than 500 appearances for Altrincham during its golden era of the '70s and '80s, Graham Heathcote knows all about the club's remarkable relationship with the FA Cup, and the giant-killing exploits that forged its identity. One of the club's most legendary figures, he believes they can inspire the current team to pull off another upset against League One Notts County, despite being separated by two divisions. Over the years, Altrincham - currently seventh in the National League - have defeated 17 Football League opponents in the competition, more than any other club that has spent its entire existence in non-league football. During a 14-year playing career at the club, Heathcote secured a crucial part of that history. A 100-goal midfielder in an Altrincham team that despite being part-time, managed to reach the FA Cup's third round in four consecutive seasons between 1978 and 1982. 'We had this determination' "It was an unbelievable achievement because in those days you didn't get weakened sides in the competition like you do now with the bigger clubs," Heathcote told BBC Sport. Now in his 70s, and still living in Altrincham, he added: "During that period, we actually had a better FA Cup record than any side in the old third and fourth divisions." Heathcote was at the heart of some of the club's most memorable achievements, twice helping the fifth-tier side to defy the odds with third-round draws against first division opponents; Everton at Goodison Park in 1975, and then a star-studded Spurs at White Hart Lane in 1979. An office worker at Salford docks at the time, Heathcote even scored a penalty in front of the Kop at Anfield against Liverpool in the third round in 1981. This was an era in which Altrincham also won the FA Trophy twice. So what was their secret in cups? "We had this determination, and we became feared at that time," he says. "You reach your level in football, but on a one-off occasion you'd be astonished at where you can raise your game to. You can't do it every week, but it's just a case of getting the mindset right on the day." The club may also have been fuelled by a sense of injustice. Because despite twice winning what was then the Alliance Premier League, Altrincham were victims of a ballot system that cruelly denied them progression to the Football League - by just a single vote in 1980 - before automatic promotion was introduced a few years later. Heathcote scored a penalty against Liverpool in the FA Cup in 1981 [Getty Images] 'We have a real opportunity' Heathcote had left by the time Altrincham pulled off their greatest cup exploit - knocking out first division Birmingham City at St Andrews in 1986 in what remains one of the competition's biggest shocks. They became only the second of four non-league teams to beat top-flight opposition away from home. Forty years on from that famous night, current manager Neil Gibson is all too aware of the tradition that he now hopes to continue in front of a live BBC TV audience, and a bumper Moss Lane crowd. Having joined last year to help the club avoid relegation, the Welshman has overseen an impressive start to the current National League campaign, with Altrincham looking like play-off contenders. The dream of a first ever promotion to the EFL is the priority. But Gibson is desperate to build on the recent progress against Notts County. "It would mean a lot. It's the spirit and essence of this club," he says. "We have a real opportunity. They are a very good team, but it's a game where we feel that we can go and etch our own memories. All the fans remember those cup moments from the past and we want to try and replicate that." Situated just a few miles from Old Trafford, and in an area of Greater Manchester dominated by fans of United and City, Altrincham has to work hard to maintain its supporter base. But this is a rare moment in the national spotlight for a community club that only turned professional four years ago. "A lot of our players are good enough to play at a higher level, and it's a chance to showcase themselves and test ourselves against a club that three years ago were in the same league as us," says Gibson, whose squad includes five players that have previously appeared for Notts County. Gibson has real cup pedigree of his own to draw upon, including against Saturday's opponents. 24 years ago, he played for Conference club Southport as they produced a memorable FA Cup upset over Notts County. He was part of the Tranmere squad that reached the League Cup final in 2000, and he also won the Welsh Cup three times, including twice as a manager. "Cups have always been very special to me," he says. "We're really excited about it and we're going to give it absolutely everything. But you only remember these days if you come out on the right side of the result." Like father, like son Sam Heathcote followed his father by also playing for Altrincham, before moving to Macclesfield [The Heatcote Family] As for Heathcote, he also managed Altrincham - between 2002 and 2009. And in a remarkable twist of fate, his special connection with the competition has been carried on by his son. Not content with emulating his father by also playing for Altrincham, Sam Heathcote then helped them to beat League One Barnsley in 2015, the club's most recent cup upset. And as if that was not enough, having joined local rivals Macclesfield, this year Sam was at the heart of the defence for the National League North side as they stunned then-holders Crystal Palace to produce the greatest shock in FA Cup history, with a staggering 117 places between the sides. "That far exceeded anything I've done," says Graham, when asked how he explains the Heathcotes' record in the cup across the generations. "I never won in the third round. It's just one of those things!" Heathcote senior will be at League One side Mansfield on Saturday where he hopes to watch Sam - who works as a teacher in Altrincham - pull off another upset for Macclesfield. But he will also be paying close attention to the action at Moss Lane, and is backing his former club to taste glory once again. "I'd love to see them get to the third round, so the current generation of Altrincham fans can feel what it's all about," he says. "51 years ago I played at Everton and people still speak about it now. These players have that chance to create such a legacy. Don't just dream about it. Make it happen." Altrincham's challenge now is to follow in his footsteps, make Notts County number 18 on their long list of scalps, and breathe new life into their reputation as non-league football's ultimate giant-killers. How to follow the FA Cup on the BBC this weekend BBC to show Cray Wanderers v Stockport & Altrincham v Notts County

item.title: ‘Hello darkness my old friend, soon you’ll be here by 5pm’ As Simon and Garfunkel never sang…
item.description: Simon and Garfunkel Back in August I contributed an article to The Mag which was entitled “The Phoney War” , it was about the lull before hostilities began at the start of the Newcastle United season. In September I contributed “All Things Bright and Beautiful” , about our promising start to the season. October’s article “Trick or Treat” arrived a little late last weekend. It raised doubts about how things are unfolding after a series of sloppy defeats. My offering this month? Fire and darkness. November starts with the dispiriting onset of darkness. As Simon and Garfunkel never sang, “Hello darkness my old friend, soon you’ll be here by 5pm.” Darkness aside, there’s been more futility than fire from our footballing favourites. Maybe we’ll see a spark from Newcastle United in West London on Saturday. As the Scots say, maybe so, maybe no. Maybe we’ll see two bald men fighting over a comb. An increasingly dull, dreary and desperate attempt to win the coveted prize of being the fourth worst team in the league by the end of the season. There’s always hope , of course, the thing that kills you. We hope that Fulham will be even more wobbly than us. We hope that we can bag a fourth win of a mercurial season in the capital this weekend. We hope that the likes of Sunderland, Coventry, Ipswich, Palace, Fulham will finish below us by the odd point or with a less embarrassing goal difference. We hope that Santa will bring us a little stocking filler in the form of a relegation berth for Man City. If so, we hope that we won’t be one of the other two trapdoor teams. We hope that it’s going to be alright. We hope Matthias Jaissle will turn it around. We hope that the Newcastle United players will get it. We hope there’s something for them to get. We hope for a couple of signings in January. We know all about hope as Newcastle supporters. We know the sorts of things we say in our brighter moments. But November darkness doesn’t encourage hope. There’s a beguiling song by an obscure folk singer Dave Goulder, entitled “The January Man”. It’s partly about the changing seasons, month by month. This month’s line is, “The poor November man sees fire and wind and mist and rain and winter air.” We can identify with that. item.content:encoded: Simon and Garfunkel Back in August I contributed an article to The Mag which was entitled “The Phoney War” , it was about the lull before hostilities began at the start of the Newcastle United season. In September I contributed “All Things Bright and Beautiful” , about our promising start to the season. October’s article “Trick or Treat” arrived a little late last weekend. It raised doubts about how things are unfolding after a series of sloppy defeats. My offering this month? Fire and darkness. November starts with the dispiriting onset of darkness. As Simon and Garfunkel never sang, “Hello darkness my old friend, soon you’ll be here by 5pm.” Darkness aside, there’s been more futility than fire from our footballing favourites. Maybe we’ll see a spark from Newcastle United in West London on Saturday. As the Scots say, maybe so, maybe no. Maybe we’ll see two bald men fighting over a comb. An increasingly dull, dreary and desperate attempt to win the coveted prize of being the fourth worst team in the league by the end of the season. There’s always hope , of course, the thing that kills you. We hope that Fulham will be even more wobbly than us. We hope that we can bag a fourth win of a mercurial season in the capital this weekend. We hope that the likes of Sunderland, Coventry, Ipswich, Palace, Fulham will finish below us by the odd point or with a less embarrassing goal difference. We hope that Santa will bring us a little stocking filler in the form of a relegation berth for Man City. If so, we hope that we won’t be one of the other two trapdoor teams. We hope that it’s going to be alright. We hope Matthias Jaissle will turn it around. We hope that the Newcastle United players will get it. We hope there’s something for them to get. We hope for a couple of signings in January. We know all about hope as Newcastle supporters. We know the sorts of things we say in our brighter moments. But November darkness doesn’t encourage hope. There’s a beguiling song by an obscure folk singer Dave Goulder, entitled “The January Man”. It’s partly about the changing seasons, month by month. This month’s line is, “The poor November man sees fire and wind and mist and rain and winter air.” We can identify with that. So can our current manager, who looked like the poor November man at the end of Monday night’s match after shaking hands with the gargoyle Moyes. If you want a giggle in November’s darkness, search up “David Moyes Dunfermline”. It should bring up an image of a Soccer Stars/Panini type sticker of a young Davey Moyes in his playing days. Be warned: it belongs on the Halloween clearance shelf. Unsettling. NSFW. We might giggle but fly old Davey has demonstrated a certain brand of English football to MJ three times these last few months. As my Mam used to say, “that’ll learn him a thing or three.” Aggregate score 7-2. Gesundheit, or something that rhymes with it. Despite the hype of the Premier League being the world’s finest, we all know the reality: there’s an awful lot of beige football. Much of what is served up is tepid soup prepared by chefs like Moyes, using ingredients from the back of the fridge and the darkest corners of the cupboards. It sustains life but does not bring joy. Welcome to Richard Masters’ soup kitchen. One bit of bread to dunk each, except for the slippery six. They’re on the “all you can eat” tariff, butter running down their greasy chins. No soup for them. They’re having steak, followed by a selection from the sweet trolley. Coffee. Brandy and cigars. Here’s the recipe for Masters’ Beige Football Soup, a tried and trusted staple of the English football diet. The main ingredients: – a pound of Pulis – five fat Sam fingers – a whiffling of Warnock’s whiskers – a measure of Moysie’s mustard – a handful of Hughes hoofball – a brace of Bruceballs. Lob in a few streaky rashers and a head of cabbage. Method: Clag it all into a pan on a low heat until tepid. Before serving, add the following to taste: – a dash of well-drilled defence – a rasher of rogue refereeing – a pinch of percentages – a layer of long-throw – a jar of “Wee Davey’s” jam – a measure of Monday night marinade – a can of barely concealed corruption – a scoop of Stoke soil, ideally harvested on a cold, wet midweek night. Enough nutritional content and calories to keep you up. Best served lukewarm from a vat of vested interests into leaking, cracked bowls, just enough to accumulate points. November: the month of fire and darkness. Maybe Matthias Jaissle can kindle fire in the hearts of our lads and us supporters. Maybe there’ll be a light in the darkness on Saturday. Maybe.

item.title: Girona-Almeria: direct duel to get closer to the top part
item.description: Girona-Almeria: direct duel to get closer to the top part The Girona team returns to Montilivi to face a challenging match against UD Almeria, the second-placed team. After twelve rounds, the Andalusians have accumulated 26 points, while Girona has 21, a five-point difference that gives the match special significance in the fight to move closer to the top positions. Girona comes into the match after suffering a 1-0 defeat at the Real Sociedad B stadium. However, prior to that, they had achieved two convincing home victories: 2-0 against FC Andorra and 5-1 against Celta Fortuna. In the previous rounds, they also drew with Tenerife (1-1) and Mallorca (0-0). Their overall record stands at six wins, three draws, and three losses, with 22 goals scored and 11 conceded. Almeria, among the best in the category Almeria arrives at Montilivi with a solid trajectory: eight wins, two draws, and two losses in the first twelve rounds, with 23 goals scored and 10 conceded. In their last five matches, they have achieved three wins and two draws. Their most recent result was a 1-1 draw at Eibar's stadium. The Andalusian team boasts an offensive duo that has gained prominence in recent weeks. Miguel de la Fuente and Sergio Arribas have scored seven goals between them in the last five rounds. De la Fuente provides a strong presence in the area and finishing ability, while Arribas contributes creativity and attacking runs from midfield. Attention will also be needed for Brian Cipenga, who has scored three goals this season, and Thalys, who has netted two. Their contributions expand Almeria's offensive options and require Girona to stay focused against the various threats posed by their opponent.

item.title: 2. Bundesliga preview: 1. FC Heidenheim vs. Hannover 96
item.description: 2. Bundesliga preview: 1. FC Heidenheim vs. Hannover 96 The 2. Bundesliga provides an intriguing encounter on the Ostalb, as Heidenheim get set to host Hannover. Both sides have experienced contrasting fortunes in recent weeks, with Heidenheim struggling to rediscover their early-season form, while Hannover will be looking to build on their first league victory under new head coach Sandro Wagner. With just four points separating the teams ahead of the 11th matchday, Sunday's meeting presents an important opportunity for both clubs to strengthen their position in the standings. 1. FC Heidenheim Heidenheim will be determined to get their promotion challenge back on track after suffering a 2-1 defeat away to Karlsruher SC last weekend. Frank Schmidt's side appeared to be heading towards a point after Alessandro Vogt equalised late in the contest, only for the hosts to snatch all three points with a stoppage-time winner. The result extended Heidenheim's winless run in the league to five matches, with their last victory coming against Holstein Kiel back in September. Despite their recent difficulties, the recently-relegated side remain sixth in the standings with 15 points from their opening ten fixtures. Their home form has also been a positive, with Schmidt's side unbeaten at the Voith-Arena this season, recording three victories and two draws from their five matches. Sunday's encounter also carries additional significance following Schmidt's announcement earlier this week that he will leave the club at the end of the 2026/27 campaign, bringing an end to his remarkable spell of almost 20 years in charge. Speaking ahead of the Hannover fixture, Schmidt acknowledged the quality within the opposition ranks but expects an intensely contested encounter. "Accordingly, Sunday will be a real battle," Schmidt explained, highlighting the importance of intensity, second balls and winning individual duels. The Heidenheim coach also admitted that his team had been overrun in certain situations during their defeat to Karlsruhe, insisting that his players needed to rediscover their sharpness in training before returning to home action. With their unbeaten home record on the line, Schmidt will be hoping his side can produce a response and return to winning ways. Hannover 96 Hannover travel to Heidenheim with renewed confidence after finally securing their first league victory under Sandro Wagner last weekend. The victory was particularly important following a difficult start to Wagner's tenure, which had seen Hannover struggle to translate their attacking potential into consistent results. The result extended Heidenheim's winless run in the league to five matches, with their last victory coming against Holstein Kiel back in September. Despite their recent difficulties, the recently-relegated side remain sixth in the standings with 15 points from their opening ten fixtures. Their home form has also been a positive, with Schmidt's side unbeaten at the Voith-Arena this season, recording three victories and two draws from their five matches. Sunday's encounter also carries additional significance following Schmidt's announcement earlier this week that he will leave the club at the end of the 2026/27 campaign, bringing an end to his remarkable spell of almost 20 years in charge. Speaking ahead of the Hannover fixture, Schmidt acknowledged the quality within the opposition ranks but expects an intensely contested encounter. "Accordingly, Sunday will be a real battle," Schmidt explained, highlighting the importance of intensity, second balls and winning individual duels. The Heidenheim coach also admitted that his team had been overrun in certain situations during their defeat to Karlsruhe, insisting that his players needed to rediscover their sharpness in training before returning to home action. With their unbeaten home record on the line, Schmidt will be hoping his side can produce a response and return to winning ways. Hannover 96 Hannover travel to Heidenheim with renewed confidence after finally securing their first league victory under Sandro Wagner last weekend. The Lower Saxony outfit came from behind to defeat Dynamo Dresden 2-1, with Husseyn Chakroun and Marcel Hartel both scoring within seven second-half minutes to turn the contest around. The victory was particularly important following a difficult start to Wagner's tenure, which had seen Hannover struggle to translate their attacking potential into consistent results. Having collected just 11 points from their opening ten league matches, Hannover currently occupy 11th position, leaving them four points behind Sunday's opponents. Wagner will be encouraged by the character his players demonstrated against Dresden, particularly after falling behind during a difficult opening period. However, their away form remains a significant concern, with their only victory on the road this season coming against Darmstadt. They have lost their other four away fixtures. Speaking ahead of the trip to Baden-Württemberg, Wagner was full of praise for the opposition, describing Heidenheim as a "top team in the second division". The Hannover coach also highlighted their distinctive playing style, organisation at set-pieces and attacking presence inside the penalty area, acknowledging that his side face a significant challenge. Wagner will also be hoping to get more out of Benjamin Källman, who has struggled to replicate the goalscoring form that saw him register 14 goals last season. The Finnish forward has yet to find the net in the current campaign, although his manager remains pleased with his overall contribution. Nevertheless, last weekend's comeback victory provides Hannover with an opportunity to build some momentum, and another positive result would represent a significant step forward under their new coach. Head-to-head record Heidenheim have historically enjoyed the better of this fixture, winning six of the ten previous meetings between the clubs, compared to Hannover's four victories. Interestingly, none of their ten encounters in the 2. Bundesliga have ended in a draw. The hosts will also take confidence from their recent record at the Voith-Arena, having won each of their last four home meetings with Hannover. Their previous encounter came during the 2022/23 campaign, when Heidenheim secured a convincing 3-0 victory away from home, with Tim Kleindienst among the goalscorers. Hannover's last victory against Heidenheim came in August 2021, when they recorded a 1-0 home success. Team news Heidenheim have relatively few injury concerns heading into Sunday's fixture, with Luca Kerber the only confirmed absentee. The midfielder continues to struggle with muscular problems and will not be available for selection. However, Schmidt confirmed during Friday's press conference that the remainder of his squad had been involved in training. Hannover have a slightly longer injury list, with Lars Gindorf, Benedikt Pichler, and Karl Steinmann all ruled out. There is more encouraging news regarding Husseyn Chakroun, who suffered a shoulder injury during the Dresden encounter. Wagner confirmed that the attacker would be included in the travelling squad, although a decision on whether he starts or features from the bench will be made closer to kick-off. Predicted lineups 1. FC Heidenheim (4-2-2-2): Dähne; Mhamdi, Mainka, Föhrenbach, Heule; Hennrich, Schöppner; Costly, Conteh; Zivzivadze, Kaufmann Hannover 96 (3-4-2-1): Weinkauf; Ghita, Tomiak, Hugonet; Neubauer, Thordarson, Sahiti, Matsuda; Chakroun, Hartel; Källman.

VfL Bochum Bochum head into Sunday's encounter with renewed confidence after ending their difficult run of league form with a 2-1 victory away to Energie Cottbus last weekend. Uwe Rösler's side had endured a five-game winless run in the league before travelling to Cottbus, but Christian Rasmussen's late winner secured three valuable points and lifted the club to 11th in the standings. The victory was particularly important given Bochum's struggles in front of goal this season. Having scored just eight times in their opening ten league matches, they currently possess the lowest-scoring attack in the division. However, their recent cup victory over Mainz and the comeback success against Cottbus suggest that Rösler's team are beginning to find some momentum. Rösler is nevertheless expecting a difficult afternoon against a Karlsruhe side whose intensity and attacking movement could cause problems. Speaking ahead of the fixture, the Bochum coach described Sunday's encounter as a potential 50-50 contest and warned that the visitors are one of the most intense teams in the division. The German side will need to pay particular attention to Marvin Wanitzek, who Rösler identified as Karlsruhe's standout player, highlighting his ability to find space and influence matches through both open play and set-pieces. Karlsruher SC Karlsruher SC travel to Bochum looking to build on an encouraging 2-1 victory over 1. FC Heidenheim, which brought some much-needed stability to their start under new head coach Maximilian Senft. The Baden-Württemberg outfit had endured a difficult spell before welcoming Heidenheim, having suffered a heavy 6-1 defeat away to Magdeburg immediately after an impressive 4-0 home victory against Darmstadt. However, goals from Tim Civeja and Marvin Wanitzek secured a deserved victory over the recently-relegated side last weekend, with Wanitzek's superb free-kick proving decisive. Despite that result, consistency remains a significant concern for Senft. Karlsruhe have collected 11 points from their opening ten league matches, leaving them level with Bochum, although their inferior goal difference places them two positions below Sunday's opponents. Their away form is another area requiring improvement, with the visitors yet to record an away victory in the league this season, collecting just two points from their four matches on the road. Senft acknowledged that his team must become more consistent when discussing their recent performances, explaining that the squad are still developing under his new tactical approach. "We are coming out of the Heidenheim game strengthened, particularly because of the way we performed tactically and mentally," the Austrian coach explained. He also stressed his desire to deliver positive performances more frequently rather than continuing to experience such significant fluctuations. Karlsruhe will therefore be hoping that last weekend's victory can provide the platform for a more convincing away performance, particularly against a Bochum side who have also struggled to find consistency this season. Head-to-head record Historically, Bochum have enjoyed the better of this fixture, recording 23 victories compared to Karlsruhe's 16 across 64 competitive meetings, with the remaining 25 encounters ending in draws. However, the more recent record at the Vonovia Ruhrstadion offers encouragement for the visitors. Karlsruhe have avoided defeat on each of their last six visits to Bochum, who have not beaten them at home since a 1-0 victory in May 2014. Interestingly, 13 of the 24 meetings between the sides in the 2. Bundesliga have ended in draws, highlighting how closely contested this fixture has traditionally been. The previous meeting came on the final day of the 2025/26 campaign, when Bochum claimed a 2-1 away victory thanks to Moritz-Broni Kwarteng's winning goal. Team news Bochum will be without several players for Sunday's encounter, with Enis Cokaj, Jean Manuel Mbom and Oliver Olsen having returned to training but not yet being available for selection. Babis Drakas and Philipp Strompf are also not ready to return, while Berkan Taz missed one training session earlier in the week. However, Rösler confirmed that the remainder of his squad had completed full training. The Bochum coach also suggested that changes could be made to his attacking partnership, with Philipp Hofmann having played a significant number of minutes recently. Charlie Patiño and Jarne Steuckers are among those pushing for starting opportunities following encouraging substitute appearances. Karlsruhe, meanwhile, will again be without defensive regulars Marcel Franke and Sebastian Jung, who are both unavailable through injury. New signing Héliton has completed his first full week of training since the previous international break, although Senft indicated that he is more likely to be considered for a brief appearance rather than a starting role. Paul Scholl is consequently expected to retain his place in the back three after impressing during the 2-1 victory over Heidenheim, while Tim Civeja will also hope to keep his place following his first goal in the second division. Predicted lineups VfL Bochum (4-2-3-1): Horn; Klaiber, Steinwender, Mets, Wittek; Pannewig, Meyer; Taz, Rasmussen, Miyoshi; Hofmann Karlsruher SC (3-4-2-1): Bernat; Kobald, Scholl, Trémoulet; Pinto Pedrosa, Väänänen, Civeja, Ofli; Wiethaup, Wanitzek; Fukuda

item.title: Max Eberl would love to bring £50m player to Bayern Munich
item.description: Max Eberl would love to bring £50m player to Bayern Munich Bayern Munich are expected to sign a new winger, either in the January window or next summer, and several names have been linked with a move already. One of the players who is of interest to Bayern is Antonio Nusa, who has impressed heavily at RB Leipzig in the past 15 months. Bayern were heavily linked with a move for JJ Gabriel of Manchester United , but the youngster has decided to join Real Madrid instead. Bayern Munich interested in Antonio Nusa? View this post on Instagram Christian Falk has exclusively told CFBayern Insider that Bayern had shown interest in Nusa during the summer window. Max Eberl really likes the player and would love to bring him to Bayern. The Bavarian giants are looking for a back-up for Luis Diaz in the left-wing role, but Nusa would provide direct competition to the Colombian. Falk said: “ It is TRUE: Antonio Nusa was on Bayern’s radar in the summer.Max Eberl loves this player and would really like to bring him to Bayern Munich. As I mentioned, Bayern were looking for a potential backup option to Luis Diaz, but Nusa is no “backup”. He wants frequent game time in the starting XI. Also, it’s worth noting that RB Leipzig paid €21m [£17.5m] for the Norway international; great business it has to be said. However, if Bayern Munich are at the table, €21m will not be enough. I heard that there were talks in the range of €50m-60m [£41.6m-50m]. “This would have been too much for a backup signing. So, I don’t think there’s a chance to bring Nusa to Munich next summer but in the end you have to see what happens with the other players. We’ve mentioned players who are two or three years younger and can develop. But if it doesn’t work out, like with JJ Gabriel, perhaps Nusa can come up in conversation again. Of course, negotiations between RB Leipzig are Bayern Munich typically difficult and expensive! So, I’m not sure if it will work. “ Antonio Nusa would be a fantastic signing (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) The 21-year-old joined RB Leipzig in the summer of 2024, and has made 85 appearances for the club, scoring 16 goals across all competitions. Usually, he plays on the left, but can also play on the right and through the middle, and his versatility could be an asset for Vincent Kompany. Nusa has a contract at Leipzig until 2029, and Falk has suggested that it will not be easy for Bayern to negotiate deals in their favour with their Bundesliga rivals.

item.title: Kepa Arrizabalaga set for emotional Athletic Club homecoming at San Mames as Arsenal backup goalkeeper is called up by Basque Country to face Venezuela
item.description: Girona FC v Arsenal FC - Pre-Season Friendly - Getty Images Sport Arsenal goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga is poised for a poignant return to former club Athletic Club's San Mames stadium after earning a call-up from the Basque Country representative team. The shot-stopper has been named in the Euskal Selekzioa squad to take on South American visitors Venezuela during next weekend's international friendly in Bilbao. Record-breaking keeper returns to Bilbao Osasuna manager Jagoba Arrasate has included the Ondarroa native as one of the marquee names in his 22-man selection for the clash on Saturday, November 14. Currently serving as understudy to David Raya at Arsenal following previous loan stints with Real Madrid and Bournemouth, Arrizabalaga originally departed Bilbao for Chelsea in 2018. That €80 million move to Stamford Bridge remains the world-record transfer fee ever paid for a goalkeeper. Foreign-based trio join domestic core Joining Arrizabalaga in the squad as players plying their trade outside Spain are Udinese forward Unai Gomez and Bolton Wanderers attacker Gaizka Larrazabal, while Osasuna stopper Aitor Fernandez provides competition between the posts. Arrasate has once again leaned heavily on a familiar domestic core drawn from Athletic Club, Real Sociedad, Osasuna and Deportivo Alaves. In defence, Athletic's Dani Vivian, Hugo Rincon and Johaneko Louis-Jean are joined by Sociedad trio Jon Pacheco, Igor Zubeldia and Aihen Munoz alongside Osasuna's Inigo Arguibide and Malaga's Einar Galilea. Midfield options feature Athletic's Mikel Jauregizar, Sociedad's Benat Turrientes, Alaves pair Pablo Ibanez and Ander Guevara, Osasuna's Asier Osambela and Sevilla's Jon Guridi, while Athletic star Oihan Sancet, Osasuna's Kike Barja and Racing Santander duo Inigo Vicente and Asier Villalibre complete the attack. Historic friendly honours cultural ties Organised by Basque Football Federation president Xabier Goni, the fixture marks the representative team's first appearance since defeating Palestine 3-0 in front of a record 51,396 crowd on November 15 last year via goals from Unai Elgezabal, Gorka Guruzeta and Urko Izeta. Next Saturday's contest carries deep cultural weight as it celebrates the 90th anniversary of the first autonomous Basque Government formed under President Jose Antonio Aguirre in 1936. Aguirre subsequently established the Euzkadi team in 1937 to tour Europe and the Americas during the Spanish Civil War. Venezuela also holds a special bond with the region after welcoming thousands of Basque political exiles fleeing Francisco Franco's dictatorship. Hosts defend flawless head-to-head record Arrrizabalaga will hope to earn rare starting minutes in familiar surroundings next weekend before returning to north London to resume his backup duties under Mikel Arteta after the international break. On the pitch in Bilbao, Euskal Selekzioa will look to preserve their 100 per cent historical record in what will be their fourth meeting against Venezu

item.title: Packers Get Discouraging Trade Message On Colts’ Jonathan Taylor
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts scores a touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings in the first quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers have been among the teams interested in Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, but a new assessment suggests a blockbuster deal is unlikely, even with the NFL trade deadline approaching. Green Bay’s rushing offense has struggled through eight games, yet one Packers beat writer believes the reasons go beyond who is carrying the football. And the Packers’ draft-pick situation presents another obstacle. Packers Get Discouraging Jonathan Taylor Trade Assessment The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman cast doubt on Green Bay acquiring Taylor or two other running backs mentioned as trade candidates. “I don’t see the Packers trading for a Jonathan Taylor, Breece Hall or Tony Pollard,” Schneidman wrote. The biggest issue isn’t necessarily Taylor’s talent. Schneidman argued that “the run game’s biggest problem is the blocking,” making an expensive backfield addition a questionable fix. Taylor, a former Wisconsin star and three-time Pro Bowler, might also cost a first-round pick. Green Bay already sent its 2027 first-round selection to Dallas as part of the Micah Parsons trade last year. Even if the Colts lower their demands, Schneidman questioned whether the Packers would part with two middle-round selections. He also didn’t see an obvious Green Bay player who would entice another team in a trade package. Then there’s Josh Jacobs. The veteran returned in October after spending six games on the commissioner’s exempt list and remains under an NFL investigation involving additional allegations. Jacobs said Wednesday that he isn’t concerned about missing more games. Schneidman acknowledged a longer absence for Jacobs could change the Packers’ thinking. Otherwise, acquiring Taylor would create another question: Would Green Bay keep both backs, or try to move Jacobs? He also expressed doubts about the logic of pursuing Pollard, who is at a similar career stage to Jacobs. Taylor and Hall could represent longer-term options, but fitting either alongside Jacobs would be difficult. Packers Have Reportedly Checked In on Colts’ Jonathan Taylor The assessment contrasts with reports that Green Bay is interested in acquiring Taylor. NFL.com’s Bobby Kownack reported that the Packers were among teams showing interest, citing NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and ESPN’s Adam Schefter. NFL insider Jordan Schultz also previously named Green Bay among interested teams, along with Minnesota, Denver, Cincinnati and the New York Giants . item.content:encoded: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts scores a touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings in the first quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers have been among the teams interested in Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor, but a new assessment suggests a blockbuster deal is unlikely, even with the NFL trade deadline approaching. Green Bay’s rushing offense has struggled through eight games, yet one Packers beat writer believes the reasons go beyond who is carrying the football. And the Packers’ draft-pick situation presents another obstacle. Packers Get Discouraging Jonathan Taylor Trade Assessment The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman cast doubt on Green Bay acquiring Taylor or two other running backs mentioned as trade candidates. “I don’t see the Packers trading for a Jonathan Taylor, Breece Hall or Tony Pollard,” Schneidman wrote. The biggest issue isn’t necessarily Taylor’s talent. Schneidman argued that “the run game’s biggest problem is the blocking,” making an expensive backfield addition a questionable fix. Taylor, a former Wisconsin star and three-time Pro Bowler, might also cost a first-round pick. Green Bay already sent its 2027 first-round selection to Dallas as part of the Micah Parsons trade last year. Even if the Colts lower their demands, Schneidman questioned whether the Packers would part with two middle-round selections. He also didn’t see an obvious Green Bay player who would entice another team in a trade package. Then there’s Josh Jacobs. The veteran returned in October after spending six games on the commissioner’s exempt list and remains under an NFL investigation involving additional allegations. Jacobs said Wednesday that he isn’t concerned about missing more games. Schneidman acknowledged a longer absence for Jacobs could change the Packers’ thinking. Otherwise, acquiring Taylor would create another question: Would Green Bay keep both backs, or try to move Jacobs? He also expressed doubts about the logic of pursuing Pollard, who is at a similar career stage to Jacobs. Taylor and Hall could represent longer-term options, but fitting either alongside Jacobs would be difficult. Packers Have Reportedly Checked In on Colts’ Jonathan Taylor The assessment contrasts with reports that Green Bay is interested in acquiring Taylor. NFL.com’s Bobby Kownack reported that the Packers were among teams showing interest, citing NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and ESPN’s Adam Schefter. NFL insider Jordan Schultz also previously named Green Bay among interested teams, along with Minnesota, Denver, Cincinnati and the New York Giants . He said the asking price was considered too high, although a trade remained possible. Indianapolis has already traded Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. Schultz reported Thursday that the Colts plan to revisit offers after Sunday’s game against Dallas unless a team makes an exceptional proposal beforehand. For Green Bay, the need is apparent. The Packers entered Week 10 averaging an NFL-low 60.6 rushing yards per game. Jacobs has managed 75 yards on 32 carries since returning to the lineup. Coach Matt LaFleur has suggested the responsibility goes beyond the backfield. Following Green Bay’s win over Carolina, he said inconsistent blocking details, execution and play calls have all contributed to the struggles. “I would say it was more the collective,” LaFleur said. The Packers also have other positions to consider before Tuesday’s deadline, including offensive line, defensive tackle and tight end. Spending significant draft capital on Taylor would leave fewer resources to address those needs. Taylor would provide immediate star power, but his arrival wouldn’t automatically improve the blocking in front of him. That’s the argument Schneidman raises as general manager Brian Gutekunst weighs whether to pursue a blockbuster or focus on smaller improvements. item.description: Trump Exposed Reactor Core Syndrome very much in play after Democrat landslide – and Fifa’s president may pay a price Oh baby, clamp me in your repulsive mouthparts. Sink your unusually large and venomous fangs into my abdomen. And yes, we are doing this in the White House cabinet rooms, out there in plain sight of the watching world, just a gleaming golden ball between us. But it’s fine. Probably. Now take a sip of those sweet, sweet tiny male arachnoid entrails. An exciting new study was published over the summer into the habits of the Australian redback spider. The research made headlines for its focus on reproductive behaviour, specifically the male’s urgent and very willing engagement in what is known as sexual cannibalism , AKA copulatory suicide. item.title: Where to watch Army vs. Air Force today: Channel, live stream, time, schedule for service academy game
item.description: Where to watch Army vs. Air Force today: Channel, live stream, time, schedule for service academy game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . For the first time ever, a Commander-in-Chief's series game will be played in primetime Saturday night as Army and Air Force go head-to-head. Army fell to fourth in the American Athletic Conference standings after a tough 49-22 loss to Memphis on Saturday, moving their record to 5-3. With a victory this weekend, the Black Knights could stop Air Force from stealing the CIC title, and also become bowl eligible. Air Force, meanwhile, is already a leg up after defeating Navy 14-9 earlier this season. The Falcons have had some QB struggles though, with starter Liam Szarka out for the year, and backup Evan Medders also going down with an injury two weeks ago. Can Air Force take the CIC Trophy even while hurting under center? Be sure to tune in for all the action from West Point. item.title: Aleksandar Pavlović wants to win everything with Bayern Munich
item.description: (Photo by Stefan Matzke - sampics/Getty Images) | Getty Images Aleksandar Pavlović is not interested in setting modest targets for Bayern Munich this season. The young midfielder has made it clear that the expectations inside the dressing room are as high as ever, with the club aiming to co mpete for every major trophy available. Asked about Bayern’s objectives for the campaign, Pavlović delivered a straightforward answer that should sound familiar to anyone who understands the expectations at the Allianz Arena “We want to win everything: the Champions League, the DFB-Pokal and the Bundesliga title,” Pavlović told Sport Bild’s Christian Falk and Julian Agardi (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). There is no shortage of ambition in those words, but Bayern Munich has the squad and quality to make those aspirations realistic. The Bundesliga remains the club’s domestic priority, and Vincent Kom pany will expect his team to maintain its consistency over the course of a demanding league campaign. Bayern also has unfinished business in the DFB-Pokal, a competition they have not won since 2020. Ending that drought would be another important milestone for this group. Then there is the Champions League, the ultimate measuring stick for any Bayern Munich side. Winning the competition re quires more than individual brilliance. It demands consistency, resilience, tactical discipline, and the ability to deliver when the pres sure is at its highest. For Pavlović, these are not simply lofty aspirations. They are the standards expected at Bayern Munic h. The midfielder has grown into an increasingly important part of the squad, and his mentality reflects the club’s ambitions. Wi nning one trophy would represent a successful season for many clubs. At Bayern, the expectation is to chase all th ree. Pavlović clearly understands that distinction. Now the hard part begins: turning those words into silverware. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: New, improved notifications system! item.title: Stats: Valencia manager Javier Aguirre has a less-than-favourable record against Real Madrid
item.description: Stats: Valencia manager Javier Aguirre has a less-than-favourable record against Real Madrid Real Madrid are set to take on Valencia at Mestalla later today as they look to continue their excellent form ahead of the international break. The last seven games have been a breeze for Los Blancos , with Jose Mourinho’s side putting in excellent performances. This has been crucial in strengthening belief in the project that the Portuguese manager is building at the Santiago Bernabeu . Mourinho’s men will be looking to make it eight in a row before the November international break. Standing in their way is Javier Aguirre, an experienced manager who has taken over in an attempt to save Valencia’s sinking ship. Aguirre’s struggles against Real Madrid According to Diario AS , the Mexican manager has faced Los Blancos 27 times in his career, securing just four victories. He has suffered 16 defeats and managed seven draws, giving him a win percentage of just 14.8%. Javier Aguirre has a lot of experience managing on the touchline. (Photo by Gonzalo Arroyo Moreno/Getty Images) Interestingly, two of his four victories came during his time as Osasuna manager. The first came in February 2003, when he secured a 1-0 victory over Madrid. Vicente del Bosque was Los Blancos ‘ manager at the time. Aguirre followed that up with a 3-0 victory over Madrid in April 2004. His third triumph came in April 2011, when Real Zaragoza secured a stunning 3-2 victory over Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid at the Bernabeu . His most recent victory came in 2023, when Mallorca defeated Carlo Ancelotti’s side 1-0. Can Aguirre trouble Mourinho again? Aguirre is an experienced manager who knows every trick in the book, and he can make life very uncomfortable for Jose Mourinho and Real Madrid. The Mexican is already said to be preparing with a back five ahead of the game in an attempt to stop Los Blancos ‘ attack. Mourinho will hope to make it eight defeats in a row against Valencia. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Aguirre has got the better of Mourinho on occasion, but the two sides could hardly be in more contrasting positions heading into this encounter. Real Madrid are the most in-form team in Europe, while Valencia sit 19th, battling relegation and desperately hoping for a turnaround. Los Blancos are playing their fourth consecutive away match and will hope to emerge victorious against Los Che . It promises to be an exciting battle between two experienced managers, and it remains to be seen whether Mourinho can add another defeat to Aguirre’s poor record tonight.

item.title: Barcelona fan-favourite emerges as strong option to replace injured Rodri against Atletico Madrid
item.description: Barcelona fan-favourite emerges as strong option to replace injured Rodri against Atletico Madrid Barcelona could also turn to Gavi for Sunday’s LaLiga meeting with Atletico Madrid, although Marc Bernal and Frenkie de Jong remain stronger candidates to replace the injured Rodri, reports Mundo Deportivo For now, manager Hansi Flick has several midfield alternatives available for this clash, with the decision likely to depend on multiple factors, including experience and form. This situation arrives as Rodri has been ruled out after medical tests confirmed a minor injury to his right hamstring. Barcelona announced on November 4 that the midfielder would miss the crucial La Liga fixture, leaving Flick with an important selection decision ahead of the trip to the Metropolitano. Gavi’s inclusion in the discussion is particularly interesting given his experience in high-pressure matches and his ability to adapt to different midfield roles. However, it is crucial to note that the 22-year-old should not be considered the leading candidate at this stage. Bernal and De Jong lead Barcelona’s midfield options Marc Bernal has solid grounds to replace Rodri. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As reported before, though, Bernal is the most natural replacement for Rodri . The academy graduate has already demonstrated his suitability for the role, having started against Elche, Athletic Club, Rayo Vallecano and Paris Saint-Germain this season. Furthermore, De Jong is another possibility after recovering from his injury problems. The Dutchman returned during the Clasico and subsequently started against Alaves, although he was a substitute against Aston Villa. His experience and ability to control possession offer Flick a different profile from Bernal. Gavi’s experience in decisive matches gives Flick a strong option Gavi’s case is built on his performances during the closing stages of Barcelona’s previous campaign. After recovering from his serious knee injury, the midfielder became an important option for Flick in several demanding fixtures, demonstrating that he could be trusted when the stakes were high. Gavi will bring a different profile than Frenkie de Jong and Bernal. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) He featured in the Catalan derby against Espanyol, where he operated as a left winger, before starting in tricky away encounters against Osasuna and Getafe. He also played as a central midfielder in El Clasico against Real Madrid, the match in which Barcelona mathematically secured the La Liga title. Those appearances showed Gavi’s tactical flexibility and competitive intensity. His ability to press aggressively, recover possession, and support attacking transitions gives Flick a different midfield profile from both Bernal and De Jong. As stated before, the decision will depend on the type of performance Flick expects against Atletico. Bernal offers the most natural replacement for Rodri, while De Jong brings greater experience in controlling possession. Gav

item.title: Nico Paz: Como director spills the beans on Man United target’s future amid Real Madrid speculation
item.description: Nico Paz: Como director spills the beans on Man United target’s future amid Real Madrid speculation Manchester United are laying down succession plans for their mercurial skipper Bruno Fernandes . The Portuguese’s spectacular 2025/26 campaign, during which he registered a record 21 assists in the Premier League, helped the Red Devils finish third in the league. If supporters expected the 32-year-old to continue his golden run this campaign, they have been left disappointed. Fernandes has managed five goals and just two assists in 13 games across all competitions to date, and United are subsequently 17th in the league table after nine games. It is clear that the English giants are heavily reliant on their talisman, and every time he struggles, the team hits an off note as well. With Fernandes also in the final 12 months of his contract, it is imperative that United bring in an able heir soon. Recent reports suggest that they have found a candidate in Como starlet Nico Paz . United want Nico Paz Paz has been a revelation since leaving Real Madrid to join Como in the summer of 2024. Last season, the 22-year-old registered 13 goals and eight assists in 40 games across all competitions. This campaign, the Argentine has hit a higher gear, and has already amassed six goals and eight assists in 13 appearances. United got a first-hand account of the player’s capabilities when he single-handedly destroyed them in the Champions League last week. Paz scored two goals and set up one more as Cesc Fabregas’ side secured a 4-1 win at home. The Argentine’s performance has reportedly convinced the Red Devils, but Los Blancos are looming large amid speculation of a buy-back clause. Como sporting director Carlalberto Ludi has now provided an update on the player’s future. N. Paz Page 1 of 4 1 2 3 4 Paz 100% a Como player Speaking to Radio Radio, as cited by Tuttomercatoweb , Ludi insisted that he feels sorry for Como fans because they have to deal with transfer rumours every year. He said: “I put myself in the shoes of Como’s supporters, because every November and every March – whether due to media speculation or for other reasons – it always comes up that Real Madrid are taking all their players back home.” “This year the talk is of Jacobo Ramon and, over the next two seasons, of Nico Paz.” The Italian club’s sporting director acknowledged Los Blancos’ buy-back clause in Paz’s deal, but hinted that any potential sale would be on Como’s terms. He continued: “The truth is that we struck a good deal last summer. Nico Paz is 100 per cent a Como player. Real Madrid have retained a buy-back option until a specific date during the transfer window, as is to be expected.” “It would, however, be a sale that would recognise the value of our work and would also be important for the club. item.title: TSG Hoffenheim vs. Schalke 04 preview: Underachievers clash in last game before international break
item.description: TSG Hoffenheim vs. Schalke 04 preview: Underachievers clash in last game before international break Schalke will hope to end their abysmal run before the international break as they face fellow strugglers Hoffenheim away from home. Hoffenheim After three away games in a week, Christian Ilzer's men will be back at SNP Arena on Sunday night. The Sinsheim side failed to win those fixtures in three different competitions. The defeat in Bremen ended a two-game winning streak in Bundesliga, days after they were knocked out of the DFB-Pokal by 2. Bundesliga outfit Holstein Kiel. And, on Thursday, they were very close to upset Europa Conference League winners Crystal Palace before an injury-time strike by former Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder Daichi Kamada undone them. However, Hoffenheim won their last two home games 3-0 against Lyon and Bayer Leverkusen. Team News Adam Hložek and Vladimir Coufal weren't in the traveling squad in London, but they both could make their return on Sunday. Alexander Prass, who scored Hoffenheim's goal against Palace, will be back after missing last week's defeat to Bremen due to suspension. Schalke Since the return of club football from October's international break, Schalke 04 have only picked up a single point in the Bundesliga. Miron Muslić’s men were also knocked out of the cup by 2. Bundesliga club Dynamo Dresden as they only scored one goal in their last six competitive games. On matchday 8, Schalke’s search for a first home goal was unsuccessful as they were dominated from start to finish by RB Leipzig, who lost all their previous away matches until that point. Schalke’s next two games at Veltins Arena will also be against Champions League participants VfB Stuttgart and Borussia Dortmund. Team News Soufiane El-Faouzi and Robin Gosens returned to training weeks after their head collision in the goalless draw with Köln. As it usually happens with out-of-form clubs, Muslić will be expected to once again make multiple changes to his starting lineup. item.content:encoded: TSG Hoffenheim vs. Schalke 04 preview: Underachievers clash in last game before international break Schalke will hope to end their abysmal run before the international break as they face fellow strugglers Hoffenheim away from home. Hoffenheim After three away games in a week, Christian Ilzer's men will be back at SNP Arena on Sunday night. The Sinsheim side failed to win those fixtures in three different competitions. The defeat in Bremen ended a two-game winning streak in Bundesliga, days after they were knocked out of the DFB-Pokal by 2. Bundesliga outfit Holstein Kiel. And, on Thursday, they were very close to upset Europa Conference League winners Crystal Palace before an injury-time strike by former Eintracht Frankfurt midfielder Daichi Kamada undone them. However, Hoffenheim won their last two home games 3-0 against Lyon and Bayer Leverkusen. Team News Adam Hložek and Vladimir Coufal weren't in the traveling squad in London, but they both could make their return on Sunday. Alexander Prass, who scored Hoffenheim's goal against Palace, will be back after missing last week's defeat to Bremen due to suspension. Schalke Since the return of club football from October's international break, Schalke 04 have only picked up a single point in the Bundesliga. Miron Muslić’s men were also knocked out of the cup by 2. Bundesliga club Dynamo Dresden as they only scored one goal in their last six competitive games. On matchday 8, Schalke’s search for a first home goal was unsuccessful as they were dominated from start to finish by RB Leipzig, who lost all their previous away matches until that point. Schalke’s next two games at Veltins Arena will also be against Champions League participants VfB Stuttgart and Borussia Dortmund. item.title: How will Barcelona line up against Atlético Madrid?
item.description: Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images | Getty Images Barcelona look to go into the final international break of the season with a statement win in the bag as the La Liga leaders travel to the capital for a monster top of the table clash against Atlético Madrid at the Metropolitano . Here’s how we think Hansi Flick will line up his troops for Sunday’s battle: Defense Barça are expecting to have an almost fully healthy and fit squad after the break if there are no issues during the international window, and they will also have Eric Garcia and Andreas Christensen in the squad for Sunday. But the two defenders have not trained long enough to be ready to start, so we expect the same back four in front of Joan Garcia that kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa: Pau Cubarsí and Gerard Martín at center-back, João Cancelo at left-back, and Brian Fariñas , who continues to impress since getting his first opportunity last weekend, starting at right-back. Midfield Barça will be without Rodri with a minor hamstring issue and there’s a real doubt about who will Flick choose to partner Pedri and Fermín López . Marc Bernal had a strong substitute cameo as Rodri’s replacement in midweek and has been Flick’s first backup choice to the Spain captain so far this season, but Frenkie de Jong is back to 100% and ready to step back into his favorite midfield role. We think Flick will go with the Dutchman for this one, which will likely cause a slight change of formation with a double pivot of Frenkie and Pedri and Fermín as the number 10. Attack Lamine Yamal and Raphinha shined against Villa and will be looking for another big night against Atlético’s tough defense, and we think Flick will once again trust Anthony Gordon ahead of Karim Adeyemi for this one. Possible XI : Joan; Fariñas, Cubarsí, Martín, Cancelo; De Jong, Pedri; Yamal, Fermín, Gordon; Raphinha (4-2-3-1) How do you think Barcelona should line up against Atlético Madrid? Let us know your thoughts, predictions and teams in the comments below!

item.title: Manchester City Release Special Edition Shirt in Collaboration With Blossoms
item.description: Manchester City Release Special Edition Shirt in Collaboration With Blossoms The link between local music and Manchester City fans has always been present, most obviously through Britpop legends Oasis, and now a new kit release has brought a different Greater Manchester artist to the doorstep. Stockport indie outfit Blossoms, who are also lifelong supporters of the club, have teamed up with the Blues to release a limited run of charity shirts celebrating four decades of local outreach across the region. With City in the Community celebrating its 40th anniversary during the ongoing 2026/27 season, main club sponsor Etihad Airways has stepped aside from their front-of-shirt position to make way for the band's logo on the hugely popular 2024/25 away kit. As announced on the club’s official website this week, the special charity drop puts a new spin on a modern favourite. While Blossoms take over the main shirt sponsor space across the chest, the Etihad Airways logo shifts onto the sleeve, sitting alongside a dedicated CITC logo printed inside the neck to mark the anniversary. Blossoms celebrated their fifth Official UK Number One album with 'Songs From The Wedding Cake' last month and are about to head out on a major arena tour across the country. Anyone hoping to pick up a shirt will have to act fast, with initial sizes dropping exclusively at the new flagship CityStore before further batches go on sale around their upcoming homecoming shows at Manchester's Co-op Live in November and December. Four decades of supporting Greater Manchester Founded back in 1986, City in the Community has spent 40 years delivering health, education, and social inclusion initiatives to youth across Greater Manchester, and all profits from the special shirt drop will go straight to the charity to help sustain its daily programmes and expand its reach throughout the local area. To make an even bigger impact across the campaign, Manchester City will match every fan donation made to the foundation on a pound-for-pound basis until the end of May, up to a total of £200,000. As Enzo Maresca's side keep pushing for results on the pitch, this joint effort between local musicians, sponsors, and Manchester City gives fans another brilliant reason to get behind the community off it. On the pitch, Enzo Maresca and his players will be wanting to maintain the winning performance they showed in the UEFA Champions League and a 2-3 victory at RB Leipzig , and taking those levels into their next Premier League clash away to Nottingham Forest .

item.title: Ilia Topuria Credits Brother For Saving MMA Career At UFC’s White House Card
item.description: Aleksandre Topuria (R) assists his brother, Georgia's Ilia Topuria (C), as they leave after losing the lightweight title bout against US fighter Justin Gaethje during the "UFC Freedom 250" mixed martial arts event on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington, DC, early morning on June 15, 2026. (Photo by Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Ilia Topuria is lucky to still have a fighting career after the damage he sustained at UFC’s White House card earlier this year and he owes it all to his brother. It’s only been five months since Topuria lost his UFC lightweight title to Justin Gaethje at Freedom 250 back in June, but it certainly seems longer. Topuria was a massive betting favorite to essentially punch his way past Gaethje and cement himself as the next big superstar in the sport. While Topuria is still young enough and talented enough to reclaim his 155-pound throne his star power took a serious hit. Fortunately, Topuria didn’t sustain any career-altering injuries from his brawl with “Highlight.” Gaethje did massive damage in the later rounds of the fight that basically left Topuria unrecognizable, but if it wasn’t for Topuria’s brother, Aleksandre Topuria, he may have left the White House lawn with permanent damage to his vision. Luckily, his brother stopped the fight before the start of the fifth round to save Topuria from any further punishment. It wasn’t the most popular decision, but certainly the right one. Topuria, who has recovered well and aiming for a return to action in early 2027 , credits his brother for saving his career that night in Washington D.C. Without him, Topuria doesn’t know if he would have been able to fight again. Check it out below: Ilia Topuria says he's grateful that his brother stopped him from taking more damage against Justin Gaethje: "If he wouldn't stop the fight, probably I wouldn't be able to fight again in my life. I'm so grateful with my brother." (via @AdamCatterall ) pic.twitter.com/T8nDaTfQp2 — Championship Rounds (@ChampRDS) November 6, 2026 “If he hadn’t stopped me from fighting, I probably wouldn’t have been able to fight again in my life,” said Topuria during a recent interview with Adam Catterall (shown above). “I’m so grateful to my brother for deciding to stop me because I love what I’m doing. I had a bad experience, but I still have a lot ahead of me. It would be very sad to hear from a doctor or anyone that I wouldn’t be able to fight anymore.”

item.title: Silas Demary Jr is ‘having a lot of fun’ with UConn Huskies after win over Michigan
item.description: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Silas Demary Jr is ‘having a lot of fun’ with UConn Huskies after win over Michigan appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Silas Demary Jr. is enjoying life with UConn after putting up a strong performance in the No. 4 Huskies’ 85-77 win over the No. 16 Michigan Wolverines on Friday night. Demary has been playing college basketball since 2023, going through his second season with the Huskies. This marks his senior campaign, making it his last chance to shine on the national stage and grow his stock for the NBA level. Demary certainly came through with a big night against the reigning champions Michigan, who UConn lost to in the national championship game. In 36 minutes of action, he delivered a stat line of 21 points, seven rebounds, four assists, and two steals. He shot 7-of-17 from the field, including 2-of-4 from beyond the arc, and 5-of-7 from the free-throw line. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Demary reflected on the win after the game on the TNT broadcast. Having his teammates surround him in celebration, the standout player made a clear declaration on his enjoyment being part of the winning program. “I’m having a lot of fun… more fun to come soon,” Demary said. The whole @UConnMBB squad pulled up behind Silas Demary Jr. for his postgame interview 😂 "I'm having a lot of fun… more fun to come soon." pic.twitter.com/XiHZGSVtVF — TNT Sports U.S. (@TNTSportsUS) November 7, 2026 How Silas Demary Jr., UConn played against Michigan Silas Demary Jr. looks forward to having his senior campaign be as great as it can be. Leading UConn to serious contention for the national championship would be a great feat for the senior star. Beating Michigan was a great step in the right direction for No. 4 UConn. They set the tone in the first half, outmatching the Wolverines 43-30 once halftime came around. Three players scored in double-digits for UConn in the win, including Demary. Braylon Mullins led the team with 23 points, four rebounds and one steal. He shot 5-of-12 overall, including 3-of-8 from downtown, and 11-of-12 from the charity stripe. Colben Landrew came next with 14 points and eight rebounds, while Jayden Ross provided nine points and four rebounds. The No. 4 Huskies will look forward to their next matchup, being at home. They host the Wagner Seahawks as tip-off commences on Nov. 9 at 7 p.m. ET. Related: USC star Jazzy Davidson reveals her NBA, WNBA GOATS Related: Valparaíso takes down Purdue with shocking double OT buzzer beater

item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Thierno Barry double fires Everton to comeback win against Coventry
item.description: The wildly optimistic Evertonian – if such a being exists – could not have envisaged David Moyes’ side fifth in the Premier League with Thierno Barry just behind Erling Haaland in the goalscoring chart when their transfer window closed in calamitous fashion. Yet there they sit, team and striker defying all expectations, following a stirring comeback against luckless Coventry. Frank Lampard endured a torturous night against his old club as Coventry impressed but were refused two strong penalty claims. The Coventry manager felt his team were denied a third time by the video assistant referee for an apparent handball by Barry when edging Everton ahead. Replays were inconclusive. It was the dancing French forward’s second goal of the game and 10th in all competitions this season. He also delivered a fine assist for Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall as the in-form midfielder put his latest England disappointment behind him to seal victory in convincing style. Continue reading...

item.title: Bellinghams celebrate ‘beautiful story’ as Jobe joins Jude in Tuchel’s England 2.0
item.description: Jude had asked head coach to scout Dortmund midfielder ‘It will be beautiful for Jude to have his brother close’ Thomas Tuchel has given a first England call-up to Jobe Bellingham , admitting the midfielder’s older brother, Jude, had nagged him to do so, as he set up the prospect of their family dream being realised. Tuchel’s inclusion of the younger Bellingham for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain was further evidence of his shift away from the squad that served him well at the World Cup last summer and towards a fresh dynamic for the mission to win Euro 2028. The manager has named a 25-man group for the game against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday and the one against Spain in Madrid three days after; of the 22 outfield players, only 11 were at the World Cup. item.title: Matthias Jaissle caught in the storm as Newcastle struggle without European fix
item.description: Panic building among fans as club visit Craven Cottage but head coach has resolute support of hierarchy At least Matthias Jaissle has a sense of humour. “There’s a lot of storm at the moment,” reflected Newcastle’s head coach on Thursday. A wry smile suggested he was not referring to the north-east weather. Jaissle has seen his tactics, team selection, man management and entire philosophy rubbished in recent days but, on current evidence, appears to be holding his nerve. After all, it is not Jaissle’s fault that his appointment has coincided with supporters, players and directors struggling to adjust to life without Champions League involvement. A disappointing 12th-place finish under Eddie Howe last season dictates that there are no more exciting trips to Barcelona, Paris and Marseille and, significantly, no much-needed boost to club finances. Indeed, Newcastle are finding life without last term’s continental fix so tricky that they travel to Fulham on Saturday with the disgruntled mindset of a passenger accustomed to flying business class who suddenly finds themselves stuck in a cramped, mid-row economy seat. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | You want proper football? Here are the FA Cup first-round ties to look out for
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Lampard appreciation at Everton, Glasner sparking Forest fire, Zubimendi and Kroupi in spotlight and Carrick v Emery Premier League top scorers Nothing better encapsulates the dysfunction that was Everton under Farhad Moshiri than the idea that an unknown vandal with a can of spray paint could influence the club’s managerial direction. “Pereira out, Lampard in” they daubed on a wall at Goodison Park when it appeared Vítor Pereira was in line to replace Rafael Benítez in 2022. Alarmed by fan protests, the Everton board opted instead for Frank Lampard and, while his tenure ended 12 months later with the club immersed in another relegation battle, there will be appreciation for the Coventry manager when he makes a first visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday. The connection between Lampard and Evertonians was genuine and a factor in keeping the club up in 2022. Both parties will be glad to see the other emerging stronger from those troubled times. Jack Grealish, meanwhile, will again be absent for Everton after his recent disciplinary breach, although the manager, David Moyes, said: “We will be working again with Jack soon.” Andy Hunter Everton v Coventry City, Friday 8pm (all times GMT) Leeds v Tottenham, Saturday 12.30pm Continue reading...

item.title: Scott Parker’s dramatic West Ham return leaves him struggling for words
item.description: The former midfielder with impressive managerial promotion record began with a thrilling comeback in draw at Cardiff Three days in and Scott Parker has already lost his voice. West Ham’s head coach arrived on Tuesday, watched his side fight back from 3-0 down to draw with Cardiff on Wednesday and was struggling to make himself heard when he met the media on Thursday afternoon. “It’s like in the summer holidays,” Parker said. “You put the flip-flops on for five weeks, then you come back home and you get your shoes on. You’re in a minute, you’ve got a blister on the back of your heel. It’s the same with a throat. I’ve not shouted for a little while. All of a sudden there’s shouting and it’s a bit croaky.” Continue reading...

item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. Continue reading...
